senses.definitionCN: 树木在一年生长中新增的一圈木质层
senses.example: Each annual ring in the trunk records one wet or dry season.
senses.exampleCN: 树干上的每一圈年轮记录着一个湿季或旱季。
senses.why: A tree writes the year as a physical circle. The annual ring is the year made visible in wood.
senses.whyCN: 树把年份写成一个物理的圆圈。年轮就是“年”在木头里显了形。

intro.en: Annual came from French and Latin words for 'year'. Its root annus is one of the oldest time words in the Latin family.
intro.cn: annual 来自法语和拉丁语中表示“年”的词。它的词根 annus 是拉丁语词族中最古老的时间词之一。

items.en: First recorded in the late 14th century meaning 'appointed by the year'; by about 1400 it meant 'happening once a year'.
items.cn: 14 世纪晚期最早记录，意为“按年指定的”；约 1400 年出现“每年发生一次”的意思。

items.en: From Old French annuel (12c.) or directly from Medieval Latin annualis, the adjective of Latin annus 'year'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 annuel（12 世纪），或直接来自中世纪拉丁语 annualis，即拉丁语 annus“年”的形容词。

items.en: Latin annus 'year' also gives annals, anniversary and annuity. Its adjective annalis was the older form behind annualis.
items.cn: 拉丁语 annus“年”还给出 annals、anniversary、annuity。它的形容词 annalis 是 annualis 背后的较早形式。

items.en: The Latin word goes back to Proto-Italic *atno-, related to a PIE root *at- 'to go'. The idea is a year as a going around, a circuit of the seasons.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词可追溯到原始意大利语 *atno-，与原始印欧语词根 *at-“走”有关。其想法是：一年就是走一圈，是季节的一次循环。

items.en: The deeper link to *at- 'to go' is reconstructed and supported by cognates such as Sanskrit atati 'walks'. It is generally accepted, not directly attested in Latin.
items.cn: 与 *at-“走”的更深联系属于重构，并有梵语 atati“行走”等同源词支持。这是学界一般接受的推断，并非拉丁语中的直接记录。

items.en: Modern English uses annual for events, figures, contracts, plants, publications and tree rings. Annular 'ring-shaped' is a different word from annulus 'little ring' and should not be confused with annual.
items.cn: 现代英语把 annual 用在活动、数字、合同、植物、出版物和年轮上。annular“环形的”来自 annulus“小环”，是另一个词，不要和 annual 混淆。

note.en: The look-alike group separates annual from words with similar letters but different roots; the meaning group separates yearly frequency from yearly totals.
note.cn: 形近组把 annual 与字母相近但词根不同的词分开；近义组区分“每年一次”和“按年统计”。

entries.definition: to declare a marriage or law invalid. It comes from Latin nullus 'none', not from annus 'year'.
entries.definitionCN: 宣布婚姻或法律无效。它来自拉丁语 nullus“无”，不是 annus“年”。

entries.definition: ring-shaped. It comes from annulus 'little ring', a different Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 环形的。它来自 annulus“小环”，是另一个拉丁词根。

entries.definition: a record of events year by year. It shares annus 'year' and is a true relative of annual.
entries.definitionCN: 按年记录事件的编年史。它共享 annus“年”，是 annual 的真正同族词。

entries.definition: happening once every year. It is the everyday synonym of annual and stresses the interval.
entries.definitionCN: 每年一次的。它是 annual 的日常同义词，强调时间间隔。

entries.definition: for each year, used especially of interest, pay, or rates. It is a Latin phrase and more formal than annual.
entries.definitionCN: 每年，尤用于利息、薪资或费率。它是拉丁短语，比 annual 更正式。

entries.definition: converted to a yearly rate from a shorter period. It is about calculation, not about an event happening once a year.
entries.definitionCN: 把较短时期的数据折算成年率。它讲的是计算方式，不是“每年发生一次”。

entries.definition: happening again and again. It does not specify a yearly interval, which annual does.
entries.definitionCN: 反复发生的。它不限定为一年一次，而 annual 限定年度周期。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: annus 'year', the ann- family (annals, anniversary, annuity), and the productive -ly and -ize forms.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分与同族词：annus“年”、ann- 词族（annals、anniversary、annuity），以及能产的 -ly、-ize 形式。

normal.en: annus is 'year'. Annual, anniversary and annuity all carry that circle of time.
normal.cn: annus 是“年”。annual、anniversary、annuity 都带着这个时间圆圈。

normal.en: Annually is the adverb: a meeting held annually happens every year.
normal.cn: annually 是副词：a meeting held annually 就是每年举行的会议。

normal.en: Annualized figures are yearly rates, even if the data came from one month.
normal.cn: annualized 数字是年化率，即使数据只来自一个月。

normal.en: An annual plant finishes its whole life inside one year; a perennial comes back year after year.
normal.cn: 一年生植物在一年内完成一生；多年生植物则年复一年回来。

normal.en: An annual ring is the year written in wood.
normal.cn: 年轮就是把“年”写在木头里。

abstract.en: Picture a circular track with twelve markers. Anything that finishes one full lap is annual: an event, a report, a pass, a plant, a ring of wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一条有十二个标记的环形跑道。任何跑完一整圈的东西都是 annual：活动、报告、票证、植物、木头的一圈。

abstract.en: The same circle serves as a container (a year's income) and as a schedule (a yearly meeting). Measurement and rhythm are two uses of one shape.
abstract.cn: 同一个圆圈既可以是容器（一年的收入），也可以是日程（一年一次的会议）。计量与节奏是同一形状的两种用途。

abstract.en: Annual is not 'annular'. One is about the year, the other about a ring; English spellings are close, but the Latin roots are different.
abstract.cn: annual 不是 annular。一个讲“年”，一个讲“环”；英语拼写接近，拉丁词根却不同。

examples.en: The annual meeting will be held in the main hall next Friday.
examples.cn: 年会将于下周五在大礼堂举行。

examples.en: The garden is planted with annuals every spring.
examples.cn: 这个花园每年春天都种一年生植物。

examples.en: Count the annual rings to estimate the tree's age.
examples.cn: 数年轮可以估算这棵树的年龄。

dict_mnemonic.text: “安牛”——安安稳稳的牛每年绕磨盘走一圈，一圈就是一年 → annual 每年的

root: 源自拉丁语 annus“年”（经古法语 annuel 或中世纪拉丁语 annualis），核心是“以一年为一圈的周期”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of annual: one yearly circle used as a schedule, a measuring period, a contract length, a plant cycle, a publication, a leave entitlement and a tree ring.
sensesIntro.cn: annual 的八个义项：同一个年度圆圈，可以用作日程、计量周期、合同期限、植物周期、出版物、假期额度和年轮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one full circle of the seasons, from a point back to the same point.
core.cn: 核心意象：季节走完一整圈，从某一点回到同一点。

branches.en: SCHEDULE: an event that returns on the yearly beat.
branches.cn: 日程：按年度节拍回来的活动。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT AND ENTITLEMENT: figures calculated over a year, and leave allocated per year.
branches.cn: 计量与权利：按一年计算的数字，以及按年分配的假期。

branches.en: DURATION: a pass or contract that lasts exactly one circle.
branches.cn: 期限：正好持续一圈的票证或合同。

branches.en: LIFE CYCLE: a plant that completes its life inside the circle.
branches.cn: 生命周期：在圆圈内完成一生的植物。

branches.en: OBJECTS OF THE YEAR: a yearly publication, a yearly event, and the ring written into wood.
branches.cn: 年份的物件化：年刊、年度活动，以及写进木头里的年轮。

intro.en: Annual is an adjective and noun built on the Latin year-word. English adds -ly, -ize and -ization, and compounds it with report, meeting and ring.
intro.cn: annual 是建立在拉丁“年”词上的形容词和名词。英语加 -ly、-ize、-ization，并与 report、meeting、ring 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on annus 'year': annalis 'yearly', annuus 'annual', and anniversarius 'returning yearly'. English anniversary and annuity descend from the same root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族建立在 annus“年”上：annalis“按年的”、annuus“一年的”、anniversarius“每年回来的”。英语 anniversary、annuity 同出这个词根。

items.meaning: once every year; every year
items.example: The report is published annually.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告每年出版一次。

items.meaning: converted to a yearly rate
items.example: The monthly gain was annualized to compare with other funds.
items.exampleCN: 月收益被折算成年化收益，以便与其他基金比较。

items.meaning: the act of converting a figure to a yearly rate
items.example: Annualization can make a short boom look permanent.
items.exampleCN: 年化处理可能让短暂的繁荣看起来像是长期现象。

items.meaning: yearly publications, yearly events, or one-year plants
items.meaningCN: 年刊；年度活动；一年生植物（复数）
items.example: The shelf holds old annuals from the 1920s.
items.exampleCN: 书架上放着 1920 年代的旧年刊。

items.meaning: happening twice a year, or every half year
items.meaningCN: 半年一次的；一年两次的（semi-“半”）
items.example: The committee meets on a semiannual basis.
items.exampleCN: 委员会每半年开一次会。

items.meaning: happening twice a year; sometimes confused with biennial
items.meaningCN: 一年两次的（常与 biennial“两年一次”混淆）
items.example: The journal is biannual, appearing in spring and autumn.
items.exampleCN: 这份期刊一年出两期，春秋各一次。

items.meaning: a company's official report for one year
items.meaningCN: 年度报告（公司一年一度的正式报告）
items.example: The annual report disclosed a sharp drop in profits.
items.exampleCN: 年度报告披露利润大幅下降。

items.meaning: paid holiday days allowed each year
items.example: He used his annual leave to visit his parents.
items.exampleCN: 他用年假去看望父母。

items.meaning: one year's growth layer in a tree
items.meaningCN: 年轮（树木一年的生长层）
items.example: A wide annual ring suggests a wet year.
items.exampleCN: 年轮宽说明那一年雨水多。

items.meaning: a fixed yearly payment, especially for retirement
items.meaningCN: 年金；养老金（按年支付的固定款项）
items.example: She bought an annuity for her retirement.
items.exampleCN: 她为退休买了一份年金。

definition_zh: 预期；预料；期待；提前处理
definition_en: to expect something and often act before it happens
core_image: 手在事情发生之前就先伸出去
scene: The forecast warned of frost, so the grower anticipated the cold and covered the young trees.
sceneCN: 这里 anticipate 是「预料到、预判」（第 1 个义项：预知某事将发生）；句意：预报说有霜冻，果农预料到低温，提前给幼树盖上了防寒布。场景要点：霜冻预报、果农、幼树、提前加盖的防寒布。

senses.title: Expect that something will happen
senses.definition: to expect or predict that something will happen
senses.definitionCN: 预期或预判某事将会发生
senses.example: We anticipate a rise in demand next month.
senses.exampleCN: 我们预计下个月需求会上升。
senses.why: Latin anticipare meant 'to take before'. The mind takes the future in advance, so the event is already held before it arrives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 anticipare 意为“提前拿取”。头脑提前把未来拿进来，于是事件还没到，就已经被握住了。

senses.title: Look forward to something pleasant
senses.definition: to await something with pleasure or excitement
senses.definitionCN: 带着愉悦或兴奋等待某事
senses.example: The children anticipate the first snow of winter.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们盼着冬天的第一场雪。
senses.why: Expectation can be emotional. When the future is taken in advance and enjoyed on the way, anticipate becomes 'look forward to'.
senses.whyCN: 预期可以带情绪。当未来被提前拿进来、并在路上就被享受时，anticipate 就变成“盼望”。

senses.title: Act before the event
senses.definition: to do something before someone else does, or before an expected event
senses.definitionCN: 在别人之前或预期事件之前采取行动
senses.example: The company anticipated its rivals by launching the app early.
senses.exampleCN: 公司提前发布应用，抢在竞争对手前面。
senses.why: The core 'take before' becomes an action: you take the move before the other party has a chance to make it.
senses.whyCN: 核心的“提前拿取”变成了行动：你在对手有机会出手之前，先把这一步拿走。

senses.title: Prevent by acting in advance
senses.definition: to deal with a problem before it becomes serious
senses.definitionCN: 在问题变严重之前就处理掉
senses.example: The city anticipated flooding by clearing the drains.
senses.exampleCN: 城市提前清理排水沟，以防内涝。
senses.why: If you can reach a problem early, you can remove it before it grows. Anticipation here is prevention.
senses.whyCN: 如果能在早期够到问题，就能在它长大前把它移除。这里的 anticipatory 就是预防。

senses.title: Come before: anticipate an event in time
senses.definition: to happen before something else, especially in a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在另一事物之前发生，尤指在顺序上
senses.example: The fever often anticipates the rash by a day.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧常常比皮疹早一天出现。
senses.why: The word can describe the event itself rather than a person's mind: one thing takes its place before another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以描述事件本身，而不只是人的头脑：一件事取代位置，出现在另一件事之前。

senses.title: Use or spend before receiving
senses.definition: to use something, especially money, before it is officially available
senses.definitionCN: 在正式获得之前就使用某物，尤指金钱
senses.example: He anticipated his salary and paid the rent early.
senses.exampleCN: 他预支了工资，提前付了房租。
senses.why: This is the most literal branch: you take the income before it arrives. The future resource is consumed in the present.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的一支：收入还没到，你就先拿了。未来的资源在当下被消耗。

senses.title: Answer an objection in advance
senses.definition: in argument, to raise and answer an objection before an opponent does
senses.definitionCN: 在论证中抢先提出并回答对手可能的反对意见
senses.example: The essay anticipates the strongest objection and replies to it.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章预先提出了最强的反对意见，并作了回应。
senses.why: In rhetoric you take the opponent's move before they make it, so the objection is already defused when it arrives.
senses.whyCN: 在修辞中，你把对手的那一步提前拿走；等反对真的到来时，它已经被卸了力。

senses.title: Music: sound the note early
senses.definition: in music, to play a note or phrase before its expected harmony or beat
senses.definitionCN: 在音乐中，在和声或节拍预期位置之前奏出某个音或乐句
senses.example: The melody anticipates the chord by half a beat.
senses.exampleCN: 旋律比和弦提前半拍出现。
senses.why: Music also has expected positions in time. A note that arrives early has taken its place before the pattern expects it.
senses.whyCN: 音乐也有预期的时间位置。提前到达的音，是在模式期待它之前就占了自己的位置。

intro.en: Anticipate is built from Latin 'before' and 'take'. Its anti- is not the Greek prefix meaning 'against', a common source of confusion.
intro.cn: anticipate 由拉丁语的“在前”和“拿取”构成。它的 anti- 不是希腊语表示“反对”的前缀，这一点常被误解。

items.en: First recorded in the 1530s meaning 'to cause something to happen earlier'. The senses 'forestall' and 'prevent' appear around 1600; 'foresee' in the 1640s; 'expect' in the mid-18th century.
items.cn: 最早记录于 1530 年代，意为“使某事提前发生”。“抢先、预防”约在 1600 年出现，“预见”在 1640 年代，“期待”在 18 世纪中期。

items.en: The English verb came from Latin anticipatus, the past participle of anticipare 'to take before, take up beforehand'.
items.cn: 英语动词来自拉丁语 anticipatus，即 anticipare“提前拿取、预先处理”的过去分词。

items.en: anticipare = ante 'before' + capere 'to take, seize'. The older form of ante was anti-, which is why the English word begins with anti-.
items.cn: anticipare = ante“在前”+ capere“拿、抓”。ante 的较早形式是 anti-，所以英语词以 anti- 开头。

items.en: capere goes back to PIE *kap- 'to grasp, seize', the same root behind capable, captive and capture. The image is a hand closing on something.
items.cn: capere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *kap-“抓住、夺取”，也是 capable、captive、capture 的词根。意象是一只手合拢抓住某物。

items.en: The English verb was probably back-formed from anticipation, or borrowed directly from the Latin participle. Either way, the noun and the verb entered English close together.
items.cn: 英语动词很可能是由 anticipation 逆构而来，或直接借自拉丁分词。无论哪种，名词和动词几乎是同时进入英语的。

items.en: Modern English separates 'expect' from 'prevent' and 'come before'. The word still carries the Latin idea that the future can be taken in the present.
items.cn: 现代英语把“预期”与“预防”“先于发生”分开。这个词仍带着拉丁观念：未来可以在当下被拿取。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the anti-/ante- shape; the meaning group separates foreseeing from merely waiting or preventing.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 anti-/ante- 的形状；近义组把“预见”与单纯等待、阻止区分开。

entries.definition: the feeling or act of expecting something. It is the noun from anticipate.
entries.definitionCN: 预期；期待（anticipate 的名词形式）

entries.definition: done or felt in advance of an event
entries.definitionCN: 预先的；预期性的（形容词）

entries.definition: not expected or prepared for
entries.definitionCN: 未曾预料到的

entries.definition: to think that something will probably happen. It lacks the 'act in advance' branch of anticipate.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事很可能会发生。它没有 anticipate 的“提前行动”分支。

entries.definition: to know or predict something before it happens. It stresses knowledge, not preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情发生前知道或预测。它强调认知，而不是准备。

entries.definition: to say what will happen. It is about a claim, not about taking action beforehand.
entries.definitionCN: 说出将会发生什么。它讲的是断言，不是提前采取行动。

entries.definition: to act before someone else so as to stop them. It overlaps with anticipate's 'act first' branch but is more forceful.
entries.definitionCN: 抢在别人之前行动以阻止对方。它与 anticipate 的“抢先”分支重叠，但更强硬。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ante- 'before' + capere 'take', the capere family, and the anticipation/anticipatory derivatives.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分与同族词：ante-“在前”+ capere“拿”、capere 词族，以及 anticipation/anticipatory 派生词。

normal.en: ante- means 'before', capere means 'take'. Anticipate is to take the future before it arrives.
normal.cn: ante- 是“在前”，capere 是“拿”。anticipate 就是在未来到达之前先把它拿过来。

normal.en: The anti- in anticipate is not 'against'. It is the old Latin form of ante-.
normal.cn: anticipate 里的 anti- 不是“反对”，而是拉丁语 ante- 的旧形式。

normal.en: Anticipation is the feeling; anticipatory is the style of acting ahead.
normal.cn: anticipation 是那种感觉；anticipatory 是提前行动的风格。

normal.en: Unanticipated problems are the ones nobody took in advance.
normal.cn: unanticipated problems 就是没人提前拿进来的问题。

normal.en: Anticipate demand is a business phrase: predict it and prepare stock before it arrives.
normal.cn: anticipate demand 是商业用语：预测需求，并在需求到来前备好货。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching into tomorrow and pulling an object back into today. That is the literal geometry of anticipate.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进明天，把一件东西拉回今天。这就是 anticipate 的字面几何。

abstract.en: The hand can pull in knowledge (expect), emotion (look forward), action (preempt), prevention (prepare), or money (spend ahead).
abstract.cn: 这只手可以拉回知识（预期）、情绪（盼望）、行动（抢先）、预防（准备）或金钱（预支）。

abstract.en: The word's unity is temporal: whatever is anticipated has been moved from the future into the present.
abstract.cn: 这个词的统一性在时间上：凡是 anticipated 的东西，都被从未来挪到了当下。

examples.en: No one anticipated how quickly the virus would spread.
examples.cn: 没有人预料到病毒会传播得这么快。

examples.en: The hotel anticipates the needs of families with small children.
examples.cn: 这家酒店会预先考虑到带小孩家庭的需求。

examples.en: She anticipated the question and had the figures ready.
examples.cn: 她预判到了这个问题，数据早已备好。

dict_mnemonic.text: “安提西佩特”——安提提前把西边的佩特请来，事情还没发生人就到了 → anticipate 预料、提前行动

root: 源自拉丁语 anticipare“提前拿取”（ante-“在前”+ capere“拿”），核心是“把未来提前拿到当下”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of anticipate: one 'take before' gesture applied to knowledge, emotion, action, prevention, sequence, money, argument and music.
sensesIntro.cn: anticipate 的八个义项：同一个“提前拿取”的动作，用在知识、情绪、行动、预防、顺序、金钱、论证和音乐上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches into the future and takes something before it arrives.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸进未来，在某物到达之前先把它拿住。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AND FEELING: the future is held as expectation or as pleasant anticipation.
branches.cn: 认知与情绪：未来被握成预期，或被握成愉快的盼望。

branches.en: ACTION: taking the move first, or removing a problem before it grows.
branches.cn: 行动：先拿走那一步，或在问题长大前把它移除。

branches.en: SEQUENCE: one event occupies its place before another.
branches.cn: 顺序：一个事件在另一个事件之前占住位置。

branches.en: RESOURCES: income or benefit is used before it is received.
branches.cn: 资源：收入或好处在收到之前就被使用。

branches.en: FORMAL EARLY POSITIONS: an objection answered in advance, a note sounded before its beat.
branches.cn: 形式上的提前位置：预先回应的反对意见，提前奏出的音。

intro.en: Anticipate is a Latin-derived verb. English builds the family with -tion, -tory, -ed, un- and -ly.
intro.cn: anticipate 是拉丁来源的动词。英语用 -tion、-tory、-ed、un-、-ly 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is anticipare 'take before' and anticipatio 'foretaste, expectation'. The second element belongs to the capere 'seize' family, which also gives capture and capable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 anticipare“提前拿取”和 anticipatio“预先尝到、预期”。第二成分属于 capere“抓取”词族，也给出 capture、capable。

items.meaning: he/she/it expects or acts ahead
items.meaningCN: 他/她/它预期或提前行动（第三人称单数）
items.example: She anticipates every objection before the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 她在会议前就预判了每一个反对意见。

items.meaning: expected; also used as an adjective
items.meaningCN: 预料到的；预期的（过去式/过去分词，也可作形容词）
items.example: The anticipated storm arrived at midnight.
items.exampleCN: 预料中的暴风雨在午夜来临。

items.meaning: expecting or acting ahead right now
items.meaningCN: 正在预期或提前行动（现在分词）
items.example: They are anticipating a busy season.
items.exampleCN: 他们预计会迎来旺季。

items.meaning: the act or feeling of expecting something
items.meaningCN: 预期；期待（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The hall was full of anticipation before the concert.
items.exampleCN: 音乐会开始前，大厅里充满期待。

items.meaning: done or felt in advance
items.example: The bank asked for anticipatory payment.
items.exampleCN: 银行要求预先付款。

items.meaning: one who anticipates
items.meaningCN: 预判者；提前行动者（罕见）
items.example: A good editor is an anticipator of readers' questions.
items.exampleCN: 好的编辑能预判读者的问题。

items.meaning: showing expectation; forward-looking
items.example: Her anticipative glance told him the news was coming.
items.exampleCN: 她那带有预期的目光告诉他，消息要来了。

items.meaning: not expected
items.example: The unanticipated delay ruined the schedule.
items.exampleCN: 没有预料到的延误打乱了日程。

items.meaning: in advance
items.example: The rule was applied anticipatorily.
items.exampleCN: 这条规则被提前适用了。

items.meaning: more than one expectation
items.example: Their anticipations proved wrong.
items.exampleCN: 他们的种种预期都被证明错了。

latinEntries.meaning: to take before, take up beforehand

definition_zh: 明显的；表面上的；貌似的
definition_en: easy to see or understand, or seeming to be true without being certain
core_image: 浮在水面的倒影，看得见却未必是真相
scene: From the window, an apparent crack ran across the wall, but the engineer found it was only surface paint.
sceneCN: 这里 apparent 是「表面上的、看起来像但未必真」（第 2 个义项：貌似如此）；句意：从窗口看，墙上似乎有一道裂缝，但工程师检查后发现那只是表层涂料。场景要点：窗边的墙、看似裂缝的线条、工程师的检查、只是涂料的真相。

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Easy to see or understand
senses.definition: clear and obvious to anyone who looks or thinks
senses.definitionCN: 对任何观察或思考的人来说都清楚明白
senses.example: It soon became apparent that the plan would not work.
senses.exampleCN: 很快就明显看出这个计划行不通。
senses.why: Latin apparere meant 'to come forth, be visible'. What is apparent has come out where it can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 apparere 意为“显现、可见”。apparent 的东西，就是已经走到外面、能被看见的东西。

senses.title: Seeming, but not certainly true
senses.definition: appearing to be true or real, though it may not be
senses.definitionCN: 看起来真实，但实际上未必如此
senses.example: The apparent cause of the fire was a faulty wire.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾的表面原因看起来是电线故障。
senses.why: Appearance can be deceiving. Once 'visible' is applied to evidence, apparent also means 'visible but not yet proved'.
senses.whyCN: 表象可能骗人。当“可见”被用到证据上，apparent 也就有了“看得见但尚未证实”的意思。

senses.title: Visible to the eye
senses.definition: able to be seen, especially with the naked eye
senses.definitionCN: 能够被看见，尤指肉眼可见
senses.example: The comet was apparent as a faint line in the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗彗星在天空中表现为一道微弱的光线。
senses.why: The oldest branch is optical: something comes into view. This sense keeps the physical meaning of 'appear'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的分支是视觉的：某物进入视野。这个义项保留了“出现”的物理含义。

senses.title: Legal apparent authority
senses.titleCN: 法律上的表见代理权限
senses.definition: in law, authority that a third party reasonably believes an agent has, because of the principal's conduct
senses.definitionCN: 法律上，第三人因本人行为而合理相信代理人拥有的权限
senses.example: The court found that the manager had apparent authority to sign.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定经理具有表见代理权，可以签署。
senses.why: Law cares about how things appear to a reasonable person. Apparent authority is authority that looks real from the outside, even if it is not granted internally.
senses.whyCN: 法律关心事物在理性人眼中如何呈现。表见代理权就是从外部看像真的权限，即使内部并未授予。

senses.title: Astronomical apparent magnitude
senses.definition: in astronomy, brightness as seen from Earth rather than intrinsic brightness
senses.definitionCN: 天文学中，从地球看到的亮度，而非本身固有的亮度
senses.example: Its apparent magnitude is high, but it is actually very far away.
senses.exampleCN: 它的视星等很高，但实际上离我们非常远。
senses.why: Astronomy has to separate what we see from what is. 'Apparent' marks the observer's view, as opposed to absolute magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 天文学必须把“我们看到的”与“实际是什么”分开。apparent 标记观察者的视角，与绝对星等相对。

senses.title: Apparent heir: the expected successor
senses.definition: in succession law, an heir whose right may be defeated by a later birth or other event
senses.definitionCN: 继承法中，其继承权可能因后来出生或其他事件而失效的继承人
senses.example: He was the apparent heir until a cousin was born.
senses.exampleCN: 在一位表亲出生之前，他一直被视为推定继承人。
senses.why: The heir appears to be next in line, but appearance can be displaced. The legal term keeps the 'seeming' branch.
senses.whyCN: 这位继承人看起来就是下一位，但表象可能被取代。这个法律术语保留了“貌似”的分支。

senses.title: Evident from the evidence
senses.definition: clearly shown by the available facts or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 由现有事实或证据清楚显示出来
senses.example: It is apparent from the data that sales peaked in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 从数据可以明显看出，销售在夏季达到峰值。
senses.why: Here the 'coming forth' is done by evidence: the facts make the conclusion visible, so no guess is needed.
senses.whyCN: 这里“显现”的是证据：事实让结论变得可见，不需要猜测。

senses.title: Appearance versus reality
senses.definition: in philosophy, belonging to the world as it appears to us rather than as it is in itself
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上，属于事物向我们呈现的样子，而非其本身的样子
senses.example: The apparent world of colour may not match the physical world of wavelengths.
senses.exampleCN: 我们看到的色彩世界，未必等同于波长的物理世界。
senses.why: Philosophy turns the everyday gap between looking and being into a technical distinction: the apparent is what shows itself to a observer.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常“看起来”与“实际是”的裂缝变成技术区分：apparent 就是向观察者显现出来的那一面。

intro.en: Apparent and appear are parallel borrowings from the same Latin verb, not one derived from the other in English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: apparent 与 appear 是同一个拉丁动词的平行借入，并不是英语里一个由另一个派生。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in the late 14th century through Old French aparant. The sense 'easily seen' is recorded by about 1400; 'seeming but not necessarily real' also develops early.
items.cn: 14 世纪晚期经古法语 aparant 最早记录。“容易看见”的义项约在 1400 年有记录；“看似真实但未必真”也很早发展出来。

items.en: Old French aparant was the present participle of aparoir 'to appear', which came from Latin apparere.
items.cn: 古法语 aparant 是 aparoir“出现”的现在分词，后者来自拉丁语 apparere。

items.en: apparere 'to come forth, be visible' = ad- 'to' + parere 'come forth, be visible; obey'. The same verb gives English appear.
items.cn: apparere“显现、可见”= ad-“向”+ parere“出现、可见；服从”。同一个动词也给出英语 appear。

items.en: The verb parere 'come forth, be visible' is of uncertain origin. De Vaan suggests a PIE source such as *prh-o- 'providing', but the deeper etymology is not settled.
items.cn: 动词 parere“出现、可见”的词源不确定。de Vaan 推测可能与原始印欧语 *prh-o-“提供”有关，但更深层的词源尚无定论。

items.en: The -ent in apparent is the Latin present participle ending, not an English suffix added to appear. English borrowed the whole Latin participle through French.
items.cn: apparent 中的 -ent 是拉丁语现在分词词尾，不是英语加在 appear 后面的后缀。英语是经法语借入了整个拉丁分词。

items.en: Modern English keeps two branches: 'obvious' and 'seeming'. The phrase for no apparent reason and legal apparent authority both depend on the idea of what shows on the surface.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两条分支：“明显”与“貌似”。for no apparent reason 和法律的 apparent authority 都依赖“表面上显示出来”的观念。

note.en: The look-alike group separates apparent from its Latin siblings; the meaning group separates 'clearly true' from 'merely seeming'.
note.cn: 形近组把 apparent 与拉丁同族词分开；近义组区分“明显为真”与“只是看起来”。

entries.definition: seemingly; also, according to what is known. It often signals that the speaker is reporting an appearance, not a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 表面上；据说。它常表示说话人报告的是表象，而非事实。

entries.definition: the way someone or something looks, or the act of appearing
entries.definitionCN: 外表；出现（同族名词）

entries.definition: a ghost or strange visible figure. It shares the Latin 'come forth' root but is a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 幽灵；幻象。它共享拉丁语“显现”词根，但是另一个名词。

entries.definition: so clear that it needs no explanation. It is stronger than apparent and usually implies no doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚到无需解释。它比 apparent 更强，通常意味着没有疑问。

entries.definition: clear because the evidence shows it. It is close to apparent in the 'obvious' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 因证据显示而清楚。它在“明显”义上接近 apparent。

entries.definition: appearing to be something, often with the suggestion that it is not really so
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像，常暗示实际并非如此

entries.definition: claimed or presented as the reason, though often not the real one. It is more formal and more suspicious than apparent.
entries.definitionCN: 声称或呈现为理由，但常非真实理由。它比 apparent 更正式，也更带怀疑。

entries.definition: existing only on the surface; not deep or thorough. It criticizes the lack of depth rather than describing visibility.
entries.definitionCN: 只存在于表面；不深入。它批评的是缺乏深度，而不是描述可见性。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin apparere 'come forth', the appear/appearance family, and the legal and astronomical technical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 apparere“显现”、appear/appearance 词族，以及法律和天文学的专业用法。

normal.en: Apparent and appear are siblings: both come from Latin apparere, not one from the other.
normal.cn: apparent 与 appear 是兄弟：两者都来自拉丁语 apparere，不是其中一个由另一个派生。

normal.en: Apparently often means 'as it seems', not 'certainly'.
normal.cn: apparently 常表示“看起来如此”，而不是“确定如此”。

normal.en: For no apparent reason means no visible reason, not no reason at all.
normal.cn: for no apparent reason 是“没有看得见的原因”，不是“根本没有原因”。

normal.en: In astronomy, apparent magnitude is brightness as seen from Earth, not true brightness.
normal.cn: 在天文学中，apparent magnitude 是从地球看到的亮度，不是真实亮度。

normal.en: In law, apparent authority is authority that looks valid from the outside.
normal.cn: 在法律中，apparent authority 是从外部看像有效的权限。

abstract.en: Picture an object half in water: you see its shape, but refraction bends it. Apparent is the bent image; the real object is underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象一件半浸在水里的物体：你看见它的形状，但折射把它弯折了。apparent 是那幅弯折的像，真实物体在水下。

abstract.en: The word always keeps a gap between showing and being. Sometimes the gap is zero (obvious), sometimes it is wide (mere appearance).
abstract.cn: 这个词始终保留“显现”与“存在”之间的缝隙。有时缝隙为零（明显），有时缝隙很大（只是表象）。

abstract.en: Law, astronomy and philosophy each formalize one part of that gap: what a reasonable person sees, what an observer sees, what the mind receives.
abstract.cn: 法律、天文学和哲学各自把这道缝隙的一部分形式化：理性人看见什么、观察者看见什么、心灵接收到什么。

examples.en: It was apparent to everyone that she had been crying.
examples.cn: 所有人都明显看出她哭过。

examples.en: The apparent calm of the lake hid a strong current.
examples.cn: 湖面看似平静，下面却藏着强劲的水流。

examples.en: For no apparent reason, the machine stopped at noon.
examples.cn: 机器在中午停了，看不出明显原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿婆认他”——阿婆一眼就认出了他，因为他的样子太明显了 → apparent 明显的

root: 源自拉丁语 apparere“显现、可见”（ad-“向”+ parere“出现”），核心是“显现出来、看得见”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of apparent: one idea of 'coming into view' branches into obviousness, mere appearance, visibility, legal appearance, astronomical observation, expected succession, evidence, and philosophy.
sensesIntro.cn: apparent 的八个义项：同一个“进入视野”的观念，分叉出明显、表象、可见、法律的表见、天文观测、推定继承、证据显示和哲学现象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something comes forth into view; what shows may or may not match what is.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物走到视野里；显现出来的，未必等于实际存在的。

branches.en: OBVIOUSNESS: what comes forth so clearly that no doubt remains.
branches.cn: 明显性：显现得足够清楚，不再有疑问。

branches.en: SEEMING: what looks true but may be displaced or disproved.
branches.cn: 表象：看起来真实，却可能被取代或被证伪。

branches.en: OBSERVATION: naked-eye visibility, and brightness as seen from Earth.
branches.cn: 观察：肉眼可见，以及从地球看到的亮度。

branches.en: LEGAL APPEARANCE: authority that a reasonable third party sees as valid.
branches.cn: 法律表象：理性第三人认为有效的权限。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: the world as it appears to a subject, set against the world as it is.
branches.cn: 哲学：向主体显现的世界，与自在的世界相对。

intro.en: Apparent is a borrowed Latin participle. English adds -ly and -ness, while the same Latin verb also produced appear, appearance and apparition.
intro.cn: apparent 是借入的拉丁分词。英语加 -ly、-ness，而同一个拉丁动词还产生 appear、appearance、apparition。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is apparere 'come forth', apparens 'showing', and apparentia 'appearance'. The verb parere is of uncertain deeper origin, so only the attested Latin forms are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 apparere“显现”、apparens“显现的”、apparentia“表象”。动词 parere 更深来源不确定，因此只列有文献的拉丁形式。

items.meaning: seemingly; according to appearances
items.meaningCN: 表面上；据说（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Apparently, the meeting was cancelled.
items.exampleCN: 据说会议取消了。

items.meaning: the quality of being apparent
items.example: The apparentness of the error made the apology easy.
items.exampleCN: 错误显而易见，道歉也就容易了。

items.meaning: to come into view; to seem
items.meaningCN: 出现；显得（与 apparent 同为拉丁 apparere 的平行借入）
items.example: A light appeared at the end of the tunnel.
items.exampleCN: 隧道尽头出现了一点光。

items.meaning: the act of appearing, or the way something looks
items.example: She made a brief appearance on stage.
items.exampleCN: 她在台上短暂露面。

items.meaning: to go out of sight
items.example: The ship disappeared into the fog.
items.exampleCN: 船消失在雾中。

items.meaning: the act or fact of going out of sight
items.example: The disappearance of the birds worried the villagers.
items.exampleCN: 鸟群的消失让村民担忧。

items.meaning: to come into view again
items.example: The sun reappeared after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后太阳又出现了。

items.meaning: a ghost or unexpected visible figure
items.meaningCN: 幽灵；幻象；突然显现的形象
items.example: The apparition vanished when the lamp was lit.
items.exampleCN: 灯一亮，那个幻影就消失了。

items.meaning: see-through; easy to understand
items.meaningCN: 透明的；易懂的（trans-“穿过”+ parere“显现”）
items.example: The glass is transparent enough to see the plants behind it.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃透明得能看见后面的植物。

items.meaning: the quality of being see-through or open
items.example: The government promised greater transparency.
items.exampleCN: 政府承诺提高透明度。

latinEntries.meaning: to come forth, be visible; also to obey
latinEntries.meaningCN: 出现、可见；也有“服从”义（更深词源不确定）

definition_en: an urgent request, a legal challenge to a decision, or the power to attract
core_image: 把声音送向高处，等待一个回应
scene: The community launched an appeal for clothes and books after the fire, and donations filled the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 appeal 是「募捐呼吁、公开请求」（第 6 个义项：为慈善或救助发起的呼吁）；句意：火灾后社区发起呼吁，募集衣物和书籍，捐赠物堆满了大厅。场景要点：火灾后的社区、公开呼吁、衣物书籍、堆满大厅的捐赠。

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: An urgent request
senses.definition: a serious request for help, support, or a particular action
senses.definitionCN: 为求助、支持或某种行动而发出的郑重请求
senses.example: The family made an appeal for information about the missing boy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人公开请求提供失踪男孩的线索。
senses.why: Latin appellare meant 'to call upon, address'. An appeal is a voice sent out to someone who can answer it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appellare 意为“向……呼叫、向……说话”。appeal 就是送出去、等待某个人回应的声音。

senses.title: A legal appeal against a decision
senses.definition: a formal request to a higher court to change a lower court's decision
senses.definitionCN: 向上级法院正式请求改变下级法院的裁决
senses.example: His lawyer filed an appeal against the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他的律师对判决提出上诉。
senses.why: In law the call goes upward: one court is asked to answer another. This is the oldest English sense and the source of the modern branches.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，这个呼叫向上走：请求一个法院回应另一个法院。这是英语中最古老的义项，也是现代各分支的源头。

senses.title: The power to attract
senses.definition: a quality that makes people interested, pleased, or eager to take part
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生兴趣、愉悦或参与愿望的特质
senses.example: The old market has a strong appeal for visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 这个老市场对游客有很大的吸引力。
senses.why: The call is now answered by desire rather than by duty. Something that 'calls out' to people and makes them want it has appeal.
senses.whyCN: 现在回应这个呼叫的是欲望，而不是义务。某物向人“发出召唤”、让人想要它，它就有 appeal。

senses.title: To attract or interest someone
senses.definition: to be attractive or interesting to someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人具有吸引力或引起其兴趣
senses.example: The idea appeals to young families because it is affordable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法因为价格可负担而吸引年轻家庭。
senses.why: This is the verb form of the attraction sense: the object calls, and the person answers by wanting it.
senses.whyCN: 这是“吸引力”义的动词形式：事物发出召唤，人用“想要”来回应。

senses.title: To make a formal request
senses.definition: to ask someone urgently or formally for something
senses.definitionCN: 紧急或正式地向某人索取某物
senses.example: The mayor appealed to residents to stay indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 市长恳请居民待在家里。
senses.why: The noun's request becomes an action. The speaker addresses someone with authority or goodwill and asks for a response.
senses.whyCN: 名词的“请求”变成动作。说话人向有权力或有意愿的人发出呼吁，等待回应。

senses.title: A fundraising or charity appeal
senses.definition: an organized public campaign asking for money, goods, or volunteers
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地公开募集金钱、物资或志愿者的活动
senses.example: The winter appeal raised enough coats for three hundred children.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季募捐活动募集到的外套够三百个孩子穿。
senses.why: The request is given a public shape: a campaign with a name, a cause and a target. The call becomes an event.
senses.whyCN: 请求被赋予公共形状：一个有名称、有缘由、有目标的活动。呼叫本身变成了事件。

senses.title: To invoke: appeal to reason or law
senses.titleCN: 诉诸：援引理性、法律或武力
senses.definition: to rely on a principle, authority, or force as the basis for an argument or action
senses.definitionCN: 把某个原则、权威或力量当作论证或行动的依据
senses.example: The negotiator appealed to common sense rather than to fear.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判者诉诸常识，而不是恐惧。
senses.why: Here the call is directed at an abstract authority. You ask reason, law or evidence to answer for your case.
senses.whyCN: 这里呼叫的对象是抽象权威。你请理性、法律或证据为你的主张作回应。

senses.title: A review or grievance in an organization
senses.definition: a request for a decision to be reviewed by a higher authority within an organization, or in sport
senses.definitionCN: 请求组织内更高层或体育裁判体系复核某项决定
senses.example: The club appealed the referee's decision to the league.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部就裁判的判罚向联赛提出申诉。
senses.why: The courtroom pattern spreads to any hierarchy. Wherever a decision can be reviewed, the request for review can be called an appeal.
senses.whyCN: 法庭的模式扩散到任何层级体系。只要一个决定可以被复核，这个复核请求就可以叫 appeal。

intro.en: Appeal began as a legal word for calling a case to a higher court. Its modern sense of attraction is surprisingly recent.
intro.cn: appeal 最初是法律词，指把案件叫到更高的法院。它现代“吸引力”的义项出现得晚得令人意外。

items.en: The noun is first recorded around 1300 in the legal sense of a challenge to a judgment. The verb appears in the early 14th century.
items.cn: 名词约 1300 年最早记录，法律义为对判决提出挑战。动词在 14 世纪早期出现。

items.en: From Anglo-French apeler and Old French apeler 'to call, call upon, appeal'. English took the legal usage first.
items.cn: 来自盎格鲁-法语 apeler 和古法语 apeler“呼叫、向……呼吁、上诉”。英语先接受的是法律用法。

items.en: appellare 'to address, call upon' was a frequentative of appellere 'to drive to, move toward': ad- 'to' + pellere 'drive, push'.
items.cn: appellare“向……说话、呼叫”是 appellere“驱向、推向”的反复动词：ad-“向”+ pellere“驱赶、推”。

items.en: pellere 'to drive, push' is also behind repel, expel and impulse. The appeal image is a voice or a ship driven toward a landing point.
items.cn: pellere“驱赶、推”也是 repel、expel、impulse 的词根。appeal 的意象是把声音或船只驶向某个登陆点。

items.en: The path runs from legal challenge (1300s) to a request to a person in authority (1620s), to an emotional plea (1794), to the power to attract (noun 1904, verb 1907).
items.cn: 语义路径从法律挑战（14 世纪）到向权威请求（17 世纪 20 年代），再到情感恳求（1794），最后到吸引力（名词 1904，动词 1907）。

items.en: Modern English keeps all branches at once: court, charity, advertising and sport. The same word can be a plea, a procedure and a charm.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留所有分支：法庭、慈善、广告和体育。同一个词可以是恳求、程序，也可以是一种魅力。

note.en: The look-alike group separates appeal from similar-looking words; the meaning group separates a request from the attraction it may create.
note.cn: 形近组把 appeal 与形似词分开；近义组区分“请求”和它可能产生的“吸引力”。

entries.definition: to shock or horrify someone. It looks similar but comes from a different source and has nothing to do with calling.
entries.definitionCN: 使震惊、使骇然。拼写相近，但来源不同，与“呼叫”无关。

entries.definition: attractive or moving. It is the present participle and adjective from appeal.
entries.definitionCN: 有吸引力的；动人的。它是 appeal 的现在分词兼形容词。

entries.definition: the person who brings an appeal in a court case
entries.definitionCN: 上诉人（在案件中提出上诉的人）

entries.definition: an urgent emotional request. It is warmer and more personal than appeal, which can also be formal or legal.
entries.definitionCN: 急切的情感请求。它比 appeal 更温暖、更个人化，而 appeal 也可以是正式或法律的。

entries.definition: a formal written request signed by many people. It is a document or campaign, not usually a single spoken call.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多人签名的正式书面请求。它通常是文件或运动，而不是一次口头呼吁。

entries.definition: the power to draw people or interest. It matches the 'appeal' sense but lacks the request and legal branches.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引人或兴趣的力量。它对应 appeal 的“吸引力”义，但没有“请求”和“法律”分支。

entries.definition: a serious, often humble request. It is more literary and more submissive than appeal.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重而谦卑的请求。它更书面、更低声下气。

entries.definition: the neutral word for asking for something. Appeal adds urgency, authority, or a legal procedure.
entries.definitionCN: “请求”的中性词。appeal 则增加了紧迫感、权威性或法律程序。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ad- 'to' + pellere 'drive', the appellant/appellate legal family, and the modern attraction sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分与同族词：ad-“向”+ pellere“驱赶”、appellant/appellate 法律词族，以及现代“吸引力”义。

normal.en: The word began in court: you appeal a decision to a higher court.
normal.cn: 这个词从法庭开始：你把裁决上诉到更高的法院。

normal.en: Then the call moved outward: appeal to the public, appeal for help.
normal.cn: 然后这个呼叫向外扩展：向公众呼吁、请求援助。

normal.en: The newest branch is attraction: a design or a song can appeal to you.
normal.cn: 最新的分支是吸引力：一个设计或一首歌可以吸引你。

normal.en: Appellant is the person who appeals; appellate is the court that hears appeals.
normal.cn: appellant 是提出上诉的人；appellate 是受理上诉的法院。

normal.en: Appeal to reason means ask reason to answer for your case.
normal.cn: appeal to reason 就是请理性为你的主张作答。

abstract.en: Picture a voice rising from a low place toward a high window. The voice asks; the window may answer. That vertical call is the original appeal.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音从低处升向高处的窗户。声音在请求，窗户可能回应。这道垂直的呼叫就是 appeal 的原型。

abstract.en: The same call can travel to a court, to the public, to an abstract principle, or into a person's desires. The direction changes, the call remains.
abstract.cn: 同一道呼叫可以传向法庭、公众、抽象原则，也可以传进一个人的欲望。方向在变，呼叫还在。

abstract.en: Attraction is appeal with no words: the object calls, and the body answers before the mind explains why.
abstract.cn: 吸引力是无言的 appeal：物体发出召唤，身体先回应，头脑后才解释为什么。

examples.en: The charity made an appeal for winter coats.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构发起了冬衣募捐呼吁。

examples.en: The decision was reversed on appeal.
examples.cn: 该裁决经上诉后被推翻。

examples.en: The simple design appeals to both children and adults.
examples.cn: 这个简洁的设计同时吸引孩子和成年人。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿皮尔”——阿皮站在尔山下高声一喊，山上的人回头了 → appeal 呼吁、吸引

root: 源自拉丁语 appellare“向……呼叫”（ad-“向”+ pellere“驱赶”），核心是“把声音送出去，请求回应”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of appeal: one call sent upward to a court, to the public, to a principle, or into the space of attraction.
sensesIntro.cn: appeal 的八个义项：同一道向上发出的呼叫，可以传向法庭、公众、原则，或进入吸引力的空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice is sent out toward someone or something that can answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：声音被送向某个能够回应的对象。

branches.en: THE REQUEST: an urgent call for help or action, as noun or verb.
branches.cn: 请求：为求助或行动发出的紧急呼叫，可作名词或动词。

branches.en: THE HIERARCHY: a decision is taken to a higher court or authority for review.
branches.cn: 层级：决定被送到更高法院或权威处复核。

branches.en: ATTRACTION: the call is answered by desire rather than duty.
branches.cn: 吸引力：回应呼叫的是欲望，而不是义务。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: a public request takes the shape of an organized fundraising event.
branches.cn: 运动：公开请求变成有组织的募捐活动。

branches.en: THE PRINCIPLE: reason, law or force is invoked as the authority that should answer.
branches.cn: 原则：援引理性、法律或武力作为应当回应的权威。

intro.en: Appeal is a borrowed verb and noun. English adds -ing, -ant, -ate and -ation, and uses the -able form for reviewable decisions.
intro.cn: appeal 是借入的动词和名词。英语加 -ing、-ant、-ate、-ation，并用 -able 形式表示“可上诉的”。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is appellare 'call upon', appellatio 'address, appeal', and appellere 'drive toward'. The driving verb pellere also yields repulse and expel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 appellare“呼叫”、appellatio“称呼、上诉”、appellere“驱向”。驱赶动词 pellere 还给出 repulse、expel。

items.meaning: he/she/it appeals; more than one appeal
items.meaningCN: 他/她/它呼吁；多个上诉或呼吁（三单或复数）
items.example: She appeals to the better side of her audience.
items.exampleCN: 她呼吁听众中善良的一面。

items.meaning: made an appeal in the past
items.meaningCN: 曾提出上诉或呼吁（过去式/过去分词）
items.example: The city appealed for calm after the flood.
items.exampleCN: 洪水过后，市政府呼吁保持冷静。

items.meaning: attractive or moving
items.example: The idea is appealing because it saves time.
items.exampleCN: 这个想法因为省时而吸引人。

items.meaning: in an attractive way
items.example: The room was appealingly simple.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间简洁得恰到好处。

items.meaning: not attractive
items.example: The grey cafeteria looked unappealing.
items.exampleCN: 灰色的食堂看起来毫无吸引力。

items.meaning: a person who appeals a court decision
items.example: The appellant argued that the trial was unfair.
items.exampleCN: 上诉人辩称审判不公。

items.meaning: relating to appeals or the court that hears them
items.example: The case moved to the appellate court.
items.exampleCN: 案件转到了上诉法院。

items.meaning: a name or title by which someone is called
items.meaningCN: 名称；称谓（“被叫到的名字”）
items.example: The wine has an appellation tied to its region.
items.exampleCN: 这种葡萄酒的名称与产地绑定。

items.meaning: able to be appealed
items.example: Only final orders are appealable.
items.exampleCN: 只有最终命令才可以上诉。

items.meaning: an appeal made in response to another appeal
items.example: The company filed a counterappeal.
items.exampleCN: 公司提出了反上诉。

definition_en: to come near, or a way of dealing with a problem or task
core_image: 一条逐渐收窄、通向门口的路
scene: Her advisor suggested a new approach: interview ten users first, then decide what the product should do.
sceneCN: 这里 approach 是「方法、处理思路」（第 2 个义项：解决问题的办法）；句意：导师建议她换一种方法：先访谈十位用户，再决定产品该做什么。场景要点：导师建议、新的做法、先访谈用户、后定产品方向。

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: Come near in space
senses.definition: to move closer to a person, place, or object
senses.definitionCN: 向某人、某地或某物移动得更近
senses.example: A stranger approached the gate and asked for directions.
senses.exampleCN: 一个陌生人走近大门，问路。
senses.why: Latin appropiare meant 'to come nearer', from prope 'near'. The basic picture is a path shortening between two points.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appropiare 意为“变得更近”，来自 prope“近”。基本画面是两点之间的路越来越短。

senses.title: A method or way of dealing
senses.definition: a way of thinking about or dealing with a problem or task
senses.definitionCN: 思考或处理问题、任务的方式
senses.example: We need a different approach to this problem.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要用不同的方法处理这个问题。
senses.why: A path to a place becomes a path to a solution. The route you take toward a problem is your approach to it.
senses.whyCN: 通往某地的路径，变成了通往解决方案的路径。你走向问题的路线，就是处理它的 approach。

senses.title: A route or entrance
senses.definition: a way by which one reaches a place, especially an entrance or road
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地的方式，尤指入口或道路
senses.example: The eastern approach to the castle is steep.
senses.exampleCN: 通往城堡的东侧通道很陡。
senses.why: This is the physical path made concrete. The noun names the road or opening along which the coming-near happens.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理路径的具体化。名词命名的是“靠近”这件事所沿的那条路或那个开口。

senses.title: Speak to someone about a matter
senses.definition: to speak to someone, especially to ask for something or propose something
senses.definitionCN: 向某人开口，尤指请求或提议某事
senses.example: She approached her manager about a transfer.
senses.exampleCN: 她找经理谈了调动的事。
senses.why: Socially approaching means reducing the distance between people. You move toward someone in order to speak.
senses.whyCN: 社交上的 approach 就是缩短人与人之间的距离。你向某人靠近，是为了开口。

senses.title: Begin to deal with a task
senses.definition: to begin work on a task or problem in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式开始处理任务或问题
senses.example: He approached the essay by outlining it first.
senses.exampleCN: 他先列提纲，再着手写这篇文章。
senses.why: Starting work is entering the path. The method sense becomes a verb: to approach a task is to take the first steps toward it.
senses.whyCN: 开始做事就是踏上路径。“方法”义因此变成动词：approach a task 就是朝它迈出最初几步。

senses.title: Come near in time or amount
senses.definition: to be close to a time, level, or number
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个时间、水平或数字
senses.example: The temperature approached forty degrees at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 中午气温接近四十度。
senses.why: Distance can be measured in hours or degrees, not only meters. Whatever can be close can be approached.
senses.whyCN: 距离可以用小时或度数来量，不只可以用米。凡是能“接近”的，都可以 approach。

senses.title: Aviation: the final stage before landing
senses.definition: in aviation, the phase in which an aircraft comes in toward a runway or airport
senses.definitionCN: 航空中，飞机朝跑道或机场飞近的阶段
senses.example: The pilot began the approach in heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在大雨中开始进近。
senses.why: Flying makes the path literal again: a controlled coming-near to a fixed point. The noun names the whole phase.
senses.whyCN: 飞行让路径重新变得字面：受控地靠近一个固定点。名词命名的是整个阶段。

senses.title: Come close to a state or standard
senses.definition: to become nearly equal to a quality, condition, or ideal
senses.definitionCN: 在品质、状态或理想上几乎达到
senses.example: The performance approached perfection in the final act.
senses.exampleCN: 演出在最后一幕接近完美。
senses.why: The endpoint is now a standard rather than a place. Approaching it means getting very near without necessarily arriving.
senses.whyCN: 终点现在是一个标准，而不是一个地点。approach 它，就是靠得很近，但未必抵达。

intro.en: Approach came from French and Latin words built on prope 'near'. The physical verb came first; the 'method' sense is only about a century old.
intro.cn: approach 来自法语和拉丁语中建立在 prope“近”上的词。物理动词先出现；“方法”义只有大约一百年历史。

items.en: The verb is first recorded around 1300, meaning 'to come nearer'. It replaced the older English verb neahlæcan.
items.cn: 动词约 1300 年最早记录，意为“靠近”。它取代了较早的英语动词 neahlæcan。

items.en: From Anglo-French approcher and Old French aprochier, which came from Late Latin appropiare 'to come nearer'.
items.cn: 来自盎格鲁-法语 approcher 和古法语 aprochier，后者源自晚期拉丁语 appropiare“靠近”。

items.en: Late Latin appropiare = ad- 'to' + propiare 'come nearer', from prope 'near'. The comparative form is propior, the superlative proximus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 appropiare = ad-“向”+ propiare“更近”，来自 prope“近”。比较级是 propior，最高级是 proximus。

items.en: The 'near' family gives proximity, propinquity and approximate. Approach and approximate are cousins through prope, though they took different Latin paths.
items.cn: “近”词族给出 proximity、propinquity、approximate。approach 与 approximate 经 prope 成为表亲，但走的是不同的拉丁路径。

items.en: The noun first meant 'a coming near, an arrival'. The sense 'a way or entrance by which one reaches a place' is recorded in the 1630s.
items.cn: 名词最初意为“靠近、抵达”。“到达某地的道路或入口”这一义项在 17 世纪 30 年代有记录。

items.en: The figurative sense 'a way of dealing with a problem' is recorded around 1905. It is a metaphor from the route sense, not a separate origin.
items.cn: “处理问题的方法”这一比喻义约在 1905 年有记录。它来自“路径”义的隐喻，不是另一个来源。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against reproach, which is not a relative; the meaning group separates a method from a route and from simple proximity.
note.cn: 形近组提醒 reproach 并非同族；近义组把方法、路径和单纯接近区分开。

entries.definition: to criticize someone for doing wrong. It looks similar but means blame, not coming near.
entries.definitionCN: 因做错事而指责某人。拼写相似，但意思是责备，不是靠近。

entries.definition: friendly and easy to talk to, or able to be reached
entries.definitionCN: 平易近人的；可接近的（派生形容词）

entries.definition: coming nearer; also used as an adjective for something about to arrive
entries.definitionCN: 正在靠近；即将到来的（分词兼形容词）

entries.definition: an organized system or procedure for doing something. It stresses structure, while approach stresses the direction taken.
entries.definitionCN: 做事的有组织体系或程序。它强调结构，approach 强调所取的方向。

entries.definition: the right or means of entering a place. It matches the route sense but not the method sense.
entries.definitionCN: 进入某地的权利或手段。它对应“路径”义，但没有“方法”义。

entries.definition: close in distance or time. It is the plain adjective or verb behind the physical sense of approach.
entries.definitionCN: 在距离或时间上接近。它是 approach 物理义背后的朴素形容词或动词。

entries.definition: a long-term plan for achieving a goal. It is broader and more deliberate than a single approach.
entries.definitionCN: 实现目标的长期计划。它比单次 approach 更宏大、更有意图。

entries.definition: to move near to something. It is the everyday paraphrase of the literal verb.
entries.definitionCN: 靠近某物。它是字面动词的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ad- 'to' + prope 'near', the proximity family, and the derived approachable.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分与同族词：ad-“向”+ prope“近”、proximity 词族，以及派生词 approachable。

normal.en: prope means 'near'. Approach is to move toward near.
normal.cn: prope 意为“近”。approach 就是朝“近”移动。

normal.en: The physical path becomes a mental path: the way you move toward a problem is your approach to it.
normal.cn: 物理路径变成心理路径：你走向问题的方式，就是你处理它的 approach。

normal.en: An approach road is literal; an approach to teaching is metaphorical. The same noun covers both.
normal.cn: approach road 是字面的；approach to teaching 是隐喻的。同一个名词覆盖两者。

normal.en: Approachable describes a person who is easy to come near and talk to.
normal.cn: approachable 形容一个人容易接近、好说话。

normal.en: In aviation, the approach is the final coming-near before landing.
normal.cn: 在航空中，approach 是着陆前最后一段靠近。

abstract.en: Picture two points on a map with the distance shrinking. Approach is that shrinking, whether the points are cities, people, deadlines or ideals.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上两点之间的距离在缩短。approach 就是这段缩短，无论两点是城市、人、截止日期还是理想。

abstract.en: A method is a path you can reuse. Once a route works, it becomes a procedure others can follow.
abstract.cn: 方法是一条可以重复使用的路径。一旦某条路线有效，它就变成别人也能照着走的程序。

abstract.en: Approach stops short of arrival: it names the movement toward, not the moment of reaching.
abstract.cn: approach 停在抵达之前：它命名的是“朝……移动”，不是“到达”的那一刻。

examples.en: The train slowed as it approached the station.
examples.cn: 火车接近车站时慢了下来。

examples.en: We need a more practical approach to housing.
examples.cn: 我们需要一种更务实的住房问题处理方式。

examples.en: She approached him after the talk to ask a question.
examples.cn: 演讲结束后她走过去向他提问。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿婆肉吃”——阿婆端着肉走近门口，先靠近再想办法进门 → approach 接近、方法

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 appropiare“靠近”（ad-“向”+ prope“近”），经古法语进入英语，核心是“缩短距离、走向某处”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of approach: one shrinking distance applied to places, people, time, numbers, tasks, methods, aviation and ideals.
sensesIntro.cn: approach 的八个义项：同一段缩短的距离，用于地点、人、时间、数字、任务、方法、航空和理想。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the distance between two points shrinks as one moves toward the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个点朝另一个点移动，两点之间的距离不断缩短。

branches.en: PHYSICAL AND TEMPORAL NEARNESS: space, time and amounts can all shrink.
branches.cn: 物理与时间上的接近：空间、时间和数量都可以缩短。

branches.en: METHOD: a route toward a problem becomes a way of working on it.
branches.cn: 方法：通往问题的路线，变成处理它的工作方式。

branches.en: ROUTES: an entrance, a road, or the aviation phase before landing.
branches.cn: 路径：入口、道路，或着陆前的航空阶段。

branches.en: PEOPLE: social distance shrinks when you go to speak to someone.
branches.cn: 人：当你走向某人开口时，社交距离缩短了。

branches.en: STANDARDS: one can come near an ideal without fully reaching it.
branches.cn: 标准：人可以靠近某个理想，而未必完全抵达。

intro.en: Approach is a borrowed verb and noun. English builds approachable, unapproachable and the aviation or road compounds from it.
intro.cn: approach 是借入的动词和名词。英语由它构成 approachable、unapproachable，以及航空或道路类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on prope 'near': propiare 'come nearer', propinquus 'near', and proximus 'nearest'. Approach took the propiare branch.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族建立在 prope“近”上：propiare“更近”、propinquus“近的”、proximus“最近的”。approach 走的是 propiare 这一支。

items.meaning: he/she/it approaches; more than one method or route
items.meaningCN: 他/她/它接近；多种方法或路径（三单或复数）
items.example: The road approaches the river from the north.
items.exampleCN: 这条路从北面接近河边。

items.meaning: came near in the past
items.meaningCN: 曾接近（过去式/过去分词）
items.example: The deadline approached faster than we expected.
items.exampleCN: 截止日期比我们预想得更快临近。

items.meaning: coming near; about to arrive
items.example: The approaching storm darkened the sky.
items.exampleCN: 即将到来的暴风雨让天空暗了下来。

items.meaning: easy to talk to or reach
items.example: The professor is approachable after class.
items.exampleCN: 这位教授课后很好接近。

items.meaning: difficult to talk to or reach
items.meaningCN: 难以接近的；不易交谈的
items.example: He seemed unapproachable at first.
items.exampleCN: 他起初看起来让人不敢接近。

items.meaning: the quality of being easy to approach
items.example: Her approachability made the team open up.
items.exampleCN: 她的平易近人让团队愿意敞开心扉。

items.meaning: a road leading to a place
items.example: The approach road was closed for repairs.
items.exampleCN: 引道因维修关闭。

items.meaning: in golf or tennis, a shot played as one comes toward the target
items.meaningCN: （高尔夫或网球）接近果岭或球门的击球
items.example: His approach shot landed near the flag.
items.exampleCN: 他的接近击球落在旗杆附近。

items.meaning: a light marking the path toward a runway
items.meaningCN: 进近灯；引导飞机接近跑道的灯
items.example: The approach lights were visible through the rain.
items.exampleCN: 透过雨幕能看见进近灯。

definition_zh: 合适的；恰当的；挪用；拨用
definition_en: suitable for a particular situation, or to take something for one's own use
scene: Before the interview, she chose an appropriate dark suit and put away her bold jewellery.
sceneCN: 这里 appropriate 是「合适的、合乎场合的」（第 2 个义项：符合社交场合与礼仪）；句意：面试前，她挑了一套得体的深色西装，把夸张的首饰收了起来。场景要点：面试前、深色西装、收起夸张首饰、场合得体。

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，更多用 more 构成）
最高级（形容词，更多用 most 构成）
过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: Suitable for the purpose
senses.definition: right or suitable for a particular purpose or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某一目的或情境而言正确、合适
senses.example: The committee chose the most appropriate site for the school.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会为学校选定了最合适的地点。
senses.why: Latin appropriare meant 'to make one's own, to set apart for a use'. A thing set apart for a purpose is fitting for that purpose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appropriare 意为“据为己有、划归某用途”。被划给某个用途的东西，就对那个用途合适。

senses.title: Proper for the social occasion
senses.definition: acceptable or proper in a social setting, especially in dress or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合中可接受、得体的，尤指衣着或举止
senses.example: Shorts are not appropriate for a formal wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 短裤不适合正式婚礼。
senses.why: Social life assigns things to occasions. What fits the occasion has been 'made proper' to it, which is the everyday social sense.
senses.whyCN: 社交生活把事物分配给场合。适合场合的东西，就是被“归到”那个场合里的，这是日常社交义。

senses.title: Corresponding to something
senses.definition: matching or corresponding to a particular thing, level, or need
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物、水平或需求相匹配、相对应
senses.example: The punishment should be appropriate to the crime.
senses.exampleCN: 惩罚应与罪行相称。
senses.why: Appropriate to links two things. One is assigned its proper place relative to the other, like a key fitted to a lock.
senses.whyCN: appropriate to 连接两样东西。一样东西相对于另一样被放到恰当的位置，像钥匙对上锁。

senses.title: Take something for one's own use
senses.definition: to take or use something, often without permission or unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 取用某物，常指未经许可或不公平地使用
senses.example: The manager appropriated the team's idea as his own.
senses.exampleCN: 经理把团队的创意据为己有。
senses.why: The verb is older and more literal: to make a thing one's own. When the taking is unauthorized, the neutral Latin act becomes a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 动词更古老、更字面：把某物变成自己的。当拿取未经许可，这个中性的拉丁动作就变成批评。

senses.title: Allocate money for a purpose
senses.definition: to set aside money officially for a specific purpose
senses.definitionCN: 正式划出一笔钱供特定用途
senses.example: The council appropriated two million dollars for flood defences.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会拨出两百万美元用于防洪。
senses.why: Public money is 'made proper' to a purpose by being set apart. This is the administrative branch of the same 'set apart' idea.
senses.whyCN: 公共资金被“划归”某个用途，也就是被分出来。这是同一个“划出”观念在行政上的分支。

senses.title: Cultural appropriation
senses.definition: to adopt elements of another culture, often a minority culture, without respect or understanding
senses.definitionCN: 取用另一文化（常为少数群体文化）的元素，却缺乏尊重或理解
senses.example: The fashion house was criticized for appropriating a sacred pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这家时装公司因挪用一种神圣纹样而受到批评。
senses.why: The 'take as one's own' sense becomes a debate about power: who is allowed to take, and who is erased in the taking.
senses.whyCN: “据为己有”义变成一场关于权力的争论：谁有权取用，谁又在取用中被抹去。

senses.title: Legal allocation of property or water
senses.titleCN: 法律上对财产或水资源的划拨
senses.definition: in law, to set apart or assign property, land, or water rights to a use or owner
senses.definitionCN: 法律上把财产、土地或水权划归某用途或某所有者
senses.example: The state appropriated the land for a public road.
senses.exampleCN: 州政府征用这块土地修建公路。
senses.why: Law formalizes the act of setting apart. Property is moved from general use into a designated purpose or owner.
senses.whyCN: 法律把“划出”的动作形式化。财产从一般用途转入某个指定用途或所有者。

senses.title: Archaic: belonging to a thing by nature
senses.titleCN: 古义：事物固有的、本来的
senses.definition: in older usage, belonging to something as its own proper quality
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中，作为某物自身固有的性质而属于它
senses.example: The old text speaks of the heat appropriate to fire.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古文献谈到火所固有的热。
senses.why: This is the Latin proprius 'one's own' at its most literal: a quality that belongs to a thing and cannot be detached from it.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语 proprius“自己的”最字面的用法：一种属于某物、无法剥离的性质。

intro.en: Appropriate is a Latin past participle borrowed whole. It is not English proper plus a suffix, although the two words share a root.
intro.cn: appropriate 是整体借入的拉丁过去分词。它不是英语 proper 加后缀构成的，尽管两个词共享词根。

items.en: Both the adjective and the verb are first recorded in the early 15th century, the adjective meaning 'suitable', the verb 'to take as one's own'.
items.cn: 形容词和动词都在 15 世纪早期最早记录：形容词意为“合适的”，动词意为“据为己有”。

items.en: From Late Latin appropriatus, the past participle of appropriare 'to make one's own, take as one's own'.
items.cn: 来自晚期拉丁语 appropriatus，即 appropriare“使成为自己的、据为己有”的过去分词。

items.en: appropriare = ad- 'to' + propriare 'take as one's own', from proprius 'one's own, particular'. The root is about ownership before it is about suitability.
items.cn: appropriare = ad-“向”+ propriare“据为己有”，后者来自 proprius“自己的、专属的”。这个词根先讲归属，再讲合适。

items.en: proprius also gives English proper (through Old French propre), property and propriety. Appropriate came with the ad- prefix, so its earliest sense was 'made own', not simply 'proper'.
items.cn: proprius 还给出英语 proper（经古法语 propre）、property、propriety。appropriate 带 ad- 前缀，所以最早的意思是“被据为己有”，不只是“得体”。

items.en: The path runs from 'take as one's own' to 'set apart for a use' to 'suitable for that use'. Suitability is the result of a thing having been assigned to a purpose.
items.cn: 语义路径从“据为己有”到“划归某用途”，再到“适合该用途”。合适，是某物被指派给某个目的之后的结果。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective and verb alive side by side. The verb now often carries a critical edge (misappropriation, cultural appropriation), while the adjective remains neutral.
items.cn: 现代英语让形容词和动词并存。动词现在常带批评色彩（misappropriation、cultural appropriation），形容词则保持中性。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the -ate/-ation family; the meaning group separates 'fitting' from 'proper' and 'timely'.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 -ate/-ation 词族；近义组区分“合身”“得体”和“及时”。

entries.definition: the act of taking something for one's own use, or money set aside for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 挪用、占用；拨款（appropriate 的名词形式）

entries.definition: in a suitable or proper way
entries.definitionCN: 恰当地；合适地

entries.definition: not suitable for the situation
entries.definitionCN: 不合适的；不得体的

entries.definition: right for a purpose or person. It is the closest neutral synonym of appropriate.
entries.definitionCN: 适合目的或人的。它是 appropriate 最接近的中性同义词。

entries.definition: correct according to social or official rules. It stresses conformity more than fit.
entries.definitionCN: 符合社会或官方规则的。它比 appropriate 更强调遵从规范。

entries.definition: suitable in a way that feels harmonious or deserved, often for a ceremony or moment
entries.definitionCN: 合适得和谐或应得的，常用于仪式或时刻

entries.definition: exactly suitable, especially of a word, remark, or choice. It is sharper and more literary.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好合适，尤指词语、评论或选择。它更精准、更书面。

entries.definition: happening at the right time. It adds timing, which appropriate does not require.
entries.definitionCN: 发生在恰当时间。它增加了时间维度，而 appropriate 不要求这一点。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ad- 'to' + proprius 'one's own', the proper/property family, and the appropriation pair.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分与同族词：ad-“向”+ proprius“自己的”、proper/property 词族，以及 appropriation 一对。

normal.en: The root proprius means 'one's own'. The adjective says 'this fits as if it were made for this'.
normal.cn: 词根 proprius 意为“自己的”。形容词表示“这东西合适得像专为这个场合而做”。

normal.en: The verb says 'make it mine': appropriate an idea, appropriate funds.
normal.cn: 动词表示“把它变成我的”：挪用创意、拨用资金。

normal.en: Inappropriate is the negative adjective; misappropriate is the negative verb.
normal.cn: inappropriate 是否定形容词；misappropriate 是否定动词（挪用他人财物）。

normal.en: Appropriate to means matching: a punishment appropriate to the crime.
normal.cn: appropriate to 表示匹配：与罪行相称的惩罚。

normal.en: Proper and property are relatives through proprius, but appropriate is not 'proper + ate'.
normal.cn: proper 和 property 经 proprius 与它同族，但 appropriate 不是“proper + ate”。

abstract.en: Picture a garment cut exactly to one body. It is not the most beautiful garment in the shop, but it is appropriate: made to fit this wearer.
abstract.cn: 想象一件按某个身体裁剪的衣服。它不是店里最美的，却是 appropriate 的：为这个穿的人而做。

abstract.en: The same root covers fitting and owning. What is 'mine' can be 'right for me'; what is assigned to a purpose can be 'right for that purpose'.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根覆盖“合身”与“拥有”。属于我的，可以适合我；被指派给某个用途的，可以适合那个用途。

abstract.en: When the taking ignores consent, the neutral act of making-own becomes a critique. That is why cultural appropriation is not merely 'borrowing'.
abstract.cn: 当取用无视同意，中性的“据为己有”就变成批判。这就是为什么文化挪用不只是“借用”。

examples.en: Wear clothes appropriate for the weather.
examples.cn: 穿适合天气的衣服。

examples.en: The city appropriated funds for a new library.
examples.cn: 市政府拨出资金建一座新图书馆。

examples.en: His joke was funny but not appropriate for the occasion.
examples.cn: 他的笑话好笑，但不适合那个场合。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿婆穿普利耶”——阿婆穿上普利耶给她裁的衣服，正合身 → appropriate 合适的

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 appropriare“据为己有、划归专用”（ad-“向”+ proprius“自己的”），核心是“把这件东西划给它该去的地方”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of appropriate: one act of 'setting apart as one's own' produces fit, social propriety, correspondence, taking, budgeting, cultural critique, legal allocation and an archaic sense of inherent belonging.
sensesIntro.cn: appropriate 的八个义项：同一个“划归自己”的动作，产生合适、得体、相称、占用、拨款、文化批评、法律划拨和古义的固有归属。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is set apart and made to belong to a purpose, a person, or an occasion.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被划出来，归属于某个用途、某个人或某个场合。

branches.en: FITNESS: a thing assigned to a purpose matches that purpose.
branches.cn: 合适：被指派给某用途的东西与那个用途相匹配。

branches.en: SOCIAL PROPRIETY: dress and behaviour fit the occasion.
branches.cn: 社交得体：衣着与举止符合场合。

branches.en: TAKING: making something one's own, neutrally or as cultural appropriation.
branches.cn: 取用：把某物变成自己的，中性或作为文化挪用。

branches.en: ALLOCATION: money, land and water are officially set apart.
branches.cn: 划拨：资金、土地和水权被正式分出来。

branches.en: INHERENCE: a quality belongs to a thing by its own nature.
branches.cn: 固有：一种性质按事物本性属于它。

intro.en: Appropriate is a borrowed Latin participle. English builds a large family with -ly, -ness, -ion, -or, in-, mis- and re-.
intro.cn: appropriate 是借入的拉丁分词。英语用 -ly、-ness、-ion、-or、in-、mis-、re- 建起一个很大的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is proprius 'one's own'. The family includes propriare 'take as one's own', appropriare 'make one's own', and proprietas 'ownership, property'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 proprius“自己的”。词族包括 propriare“据为己有”、appropriare“使成为自己的”、proprietas“所有权、财产”。

items.meaning: in a suitable way
items.example: She dressed appropriately for the funeral.
items.exampleCN: 她为葬礼穿得得体。

items.meaning: the quality of being suitable
items.example: The appropriateness of the remark was debated.
items.exampleCN: 那句话是否恰当引发了争论。

items.meaning: the act of taking for one's own use, or funds set aside
items.example: The appropriation of the land was challenged in court.
items.exampleCN: 这块土地的征用在地方法院受到质疑。

items.meaning: a person who appropriates something
items.example: The appropriator of the funds was never identified.
items.exampleCN: 挪用资金的人始终未被查明。

items.meaning: not suitable for the situation
items.example: The comment was inappropriate at a memorial.
items.exampleCN: 在追悼会上说那句话很不合适。

items.meaning: in an unsuitable way
items.example: He laughed inappropriately during the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 他在仪式上不合时宜地笑了。

items.meaning: the quality of not being suitable
items.example: The inappropriateness of the joke was obvious.
items.exampleCN: 那个笑话的不得体之处很明显。

items.meaning: to take money or property dishonestly for one's own use
items.meaningCN: 挪用（他人财物）；侵占（mis- 表示“错误地”）
items.example: He misappropriated company funds.
items.exampleCN: 他挪用了公司资金。

items.meaning: the dishonest taking of money or property
items.example: The audit revealed years of misappropriation.
items.exampleCN: 审计揭露了多年的挪用行为。

items.meaning: to take something back or use it in a new way
items.meaningCN: 重新取用；重新占有（re- 表示“再次”）
items.example: The community reappropriated the old factory as a studio.
items.exampleCN: 社区把旧工厂重新用作工作室。

latinEntries.meaning: to make one's own, assign to a use
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使成为自己的；划归某用途

definition_zh: 大约的；近似的；接近；粗略估计
definition_en: close to a value or quality but not exact
core_image: 用铅笔画的圆，接近圆，但不等同于圆
scene: Because of the traffic, the driver gave an approximate arrival time and told the person waiting not to rush.
sceneCN: 这里 approximate 是「大约的、近似的」（第 1 个义项：接近准确值但不精确）；句意：因为堵车，司机给了一个大致的到达时间，并让等他的人别急。场景要点：堵车、司机、大致时间、等车的人。
