最高级（形容词，更多用 most 构成）
过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: A nearly exact value
senses.definition: close to the correct number but not exact
senses.definitionCN: 接近正确数字，但不精确
senses.example: The approximate value of pi is 3.14.
senses.exampleCN: 圆周率的近似值是 3.14。
senses.why: Late Latin approximare meant 'to come near'. A number that has come near the true value, without reaching it, is approximate.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 approximare 意为“靠近”。一个数字靠近真值却没有抵达，它就是 approximate。

senses.title: A rough estimate
senses.definition: estimated roughly rather than calculated exactly
senses.definitionCN: 粗略估计，而不是精确计算
senses.example: Can you give me an approximate cost for the repairs?
senses.exampleCN: 能给我一个大致维修费用吗？
senses.why: When exact data is unavailable or unnecessary, the mind settles for a nearby figure. Approximation is practical nearness.
senses.whyCN: 当精确数据拿不到或没必要拿时，头脑就选一个附近的数字。近似是一种实用的靠近。

senses.title: Come near in space or amount
senses.definition: to come close to a place, level, or number
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个地点、水平或数字
senses.example: The population approximates eight million.
senses.exampleCN: 人口接近八百万。
senses.why: The verb keeps the physical motion of the Latin root. The quantity moves toward a mark and stops nearby.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁词根的身体运动。数量朝一个刻度移动，停在附近。

senses.title: Estimate roughly
senses.definition: to calculate or estimate something approximately
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物做近似计算或估算
senses.example: We approximated the distance by counting steps.
senses.exampleCN: 我们通过数步数来估算距离。
senses.why: This is the action behind the adjective: you deliberately stop short of exactness because a nearby answer is enough.
senses.whyCN: 这是形容词背后的动作：你有意不追求精确，因为附近的答案已经够用。

senses.title: Be similar to something
senses.definition: to be close in nature or form to something else
senses.definitionCN: 在性质或形态上接近另一事物
senses.example: Her style approximates that of the early impressionists.
senses.exampleCN: 她的风格近似早期印象派。
senses.why: Nearness can be qualitative, not numerical. One style comes close to another without becoming identical.
senses.whyCN: “近”也可以是性质上的，不一定是数字上的。一种风格靠近另一种，但没有变得相同。

senses.title: Come close to a condition or standard
senses.definition: to approach a state, quality, or standard without fully reaching it
senses.definitionCN: 接近某种状态、品质或标准，但未完全达到
senses.example: The translation approximates the original's rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 这份译文接近原作的节奏。
senses.why: Approximation admits a gap. The target is a standard, and the result comes near it while remaining a version, not the original.
senses.whyCN: 近似承认有缝隙。目标是某个标准，结果靠近它，却仍是一个版本，而不是原本。

senses.title: A mathematical approximation
senses.definition: in mathematics, a value or solution close enough to the true one for a practical purpose
senses.definitionCN: 数学中，对实际用途而言足够接近真值的数值或解
senses.example: The algorithm finds an approximate solution in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个算法几秒钟就找到一个近似解。
senses.why: Exact solutions can be impossible or slow. Mathematics formalizes 'close enough' as a legitimate result.
senses.whyCN: 精确解可能不可能求出，或求得很慢。数学把“足够接近”形式化为一种合法结果。

senses.title: An approximate account or match
senses.definition: a description or correspondence that captures the main points without exact detail
senses.definitionCN: 抓住要点但缺乏精确细节的描述或对应关系
senses.example: The map is only an approximate guide to the trails.
senses.exampleCN: 这张地图只是步道的近似指南。
senses.why: A representation can be close in outline while missing detail. Approximation here is a useful likeness, not a claim of identity.
senses.whyCN: 一个表征可以在轮廓上接近，却缺少细节。这里的近似是一种有用的相似，而不是宣称同一。

intro.en: Approximate came from Latin 'to come near'. The adjective and verb arrived at different times, and the modern numerical sense is later still.
intro.cn: approximate 来自拉丁语“靠近”。形容词和动词在不同时间进入英语，现代数值义出现得更晚。

items.en: The verb is first recorded in the early 15th century meaning 'to come near'. An earlier adjective sense 'similar' also appears in the 15th century.
items.cn: 动词最早记录于 15 世纪早期，意为“靠近”。形容词“相似的”这一较早义项也出现在 15 世纪。

items.en: The modern adjective approximate is recorded in the 1640s. The numerical sense 'nearly exact' develops later, with the modern 'approximate value' usage recorded in 1816.
items.cn: 现代形容词 approximate 在 17 世纪 40 年代有记录。“近乎精确”的数值义发展得更晚，“近似值”用法在 1816 年有记录。

items.en: From Late Latin approximatus, past participle of approximare 'to come near, approach'.
items.cn: 来自晚期拉丁语 approximatus，即 approximare“靠近、接近”的过去分词。

items.en: approximare = ad- 'to' + proximare 'come near', from proximus 'nearest', the superlative of prope 'near'.
items.cn: approximare = ad-“向”+ proximare“靠近”，后者来自 proximus“最近的”，即 prope“近”的最高级。

items.en: The same prope family gives proximity, propinquity and approach. Approximate and approach are close relatives, but approach came through the verb propiare while approximate came through proximus.
items.cn: 同一个 prope 词族给出 proximity、propinquity、approach。approximate 与 approach 是近亲，但 approach 经由动词 propiare，approximate 经由 proximus。

items.en: Modern English uses approximate as an adjective, verb and mathematical term. The adverb approximately is the everyday hedge: 'about', 'roughly'.
items.cn: 现代英语把 approximate 用作形容词、动词和数学术语。副词 approximately 是日常的模糊限定词：“大约、大致”。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the -ate/-ation/-ity endings; the meaning group ranks degrees of exactness.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 -ate/-ation/-ity 词尾；近义组按精确程度排列。

entries.definition: about; roughly. It is the adverb form and the most common hedge in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 大约；大致。它是副词形式，也是口语中最常见的模糊限定。

entries.definition: a value or description that is close but not exact
entries.definitionCN: 近似值；近似描述（形容词的名词形式）

entries.definition: nearness in space or time. It shares proximus but is a noun about distance, not about exactness.
entries.definitionCN: 空间或时间上的接近。它共享 proximus，但讲的是距离，不是精确度。

entries.definition: not exact or detailed. It is more informal and can imply a much wider margin than approximate.
entries.definitionCN: 不精确、不详细。它更口语，误差范围可能比 approximate 大得多。

entries.definition: based on calculation or judgment rather than exact measurement. It stresses the act of estimating.
entries.definitionCN: 基于计算或判断而非精确测量。它强调估算这个动作。

entries.definition: close in distance or time. It does not by itself imply a numerical value.
entries.definitionCN: 在距离或时间上接近。它本身不暗示数值。

entries.definition: not completely accurate. It is a negative judgment, while approximate is often a neutral description.
entries.definitionCN: 不完全准确。它带否定判断，而 approximate 常为中性描述。

entries.definition: near in value or space. It is broader and more everyday than approximate.
entries.definitionCN: 在数值或空间上接近。它比 approximate 更宽泛、更日常。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ad- 'to' + proximus 'nearest', the proximity family, and the everyday adverb approximately.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分与同族词：ad-“向”+ proximus“最近的”、proximity 词族，以及日常副词 approximately。

normal.en: proximus means 'nearest'. Approximate is the value that has come nearest without hitting the mark.
normal.cn: proximus 意为“最近的”。approximate 就是靠得最近、却没有正中靶心的那个值。

normal.en: Approximately is the everyday word: approximately ten minutes, approximately fifty people.
normal.cn: approximately 是日常用词：大约十分钟、大约五十人。

normal.en: Approach and approximate are cousins: both go back to prope 'near'.
normal.cn: approach 和 approximate 是表亲：两者都可追溯到 prope“近”。

normal.en: An approximate solution is not a wrong answer; it is an answer close enough to use.
normal.cn: 近似解不是错误答案，而是足够接近、可以使用的答案。

normal.en: The map is approximate when it shows the main roads but not every turn.
normal.cn: 当地图只画出主要道路、不标每个转弯时，它就是 approximate 的。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil circle drawn over a perfect circle. It never coincides, yet it is recognizably the same shape. That gap is approximation.
abstract.cn: 想象用铅笔在一个完美的圆上画一个圆。它从不完全重合，却一眼可辨是同一个形状。那道缝隙就是近似。

abstract.en: Approximation is not failure. It is a deliberate trade: exactness given up in exchange for speed, simplicity, or usability.
abstract.cn: 近似不是失败。它是一种有意的交换：放弃精确，换取速度、简洁或可用性。

abstract.en: The word moves between number, space, style and standard. In every case, something has come near a target without becoming it.
abstract.cn: 这个词在数字、空间、风格和标准之间移动。每一种情况下，某物都靠近了目标，却没有变成目标。

examples.en: The approximate distance between the two towns is twenty kilometres.
examples.cn: 两镇之间的近似距离是二十公里。

examples.en: She approximated the cost before asking for a formal quote.
examples.cn: 在要求正式报价之前，她先估算了费用。

examples.en: The model gives an approximate answer, not an exact one.
examples.cn: 这个模型给出的是近似答案，不是精确答案。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿婆若克西”——阿婆说若克西大约十点到，没说准，只说了个大概 → approximate 大约的

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 approximare“靠近”（ad-“向”+ proximus“最近的”），核心是“靠近目标但未完全抵达”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of approximate: one movement toward a target stops nearby, producing a number, an estimate, a likeness, a standard, a solution or a map.
sensesIntro.cn: approximate 的八个义项：同一段朝目标移动的过程停在附近，于是产生数字、估算、相似、标准、解或地图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something comes close to a target and stops short of exact coincidence.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物靠近目标，停在完全重合之前。

branches.en: NUMBERS: a value or cost close to the true one, offered as a practical answer.
branches.cn: 数字：接近真值的数值或费用，作为实用答案给出。

branches.en: MOTION AND CALCULATION: quantities move toward a mark, or are deliberately estimated.
branches.cn: 运动与计算：数量朝刻度移动，或被有意估算。

branches.en: LIKENESS: style, rhythm or quality comes near another without becoming identical.
branches.cn: 相似：风格、节奏或品质靠近另一种，却没有变得相同。

branches.en: MATHEMATICS: 'close enough' is formalized as a legitimate solution.
branches.cn: 数学：把“足够接近”形式化为合法解。

branches.en: REPRESENTATION: a map or account captures the outline and admits missing detail.
branches.cn: 表征：地图或描述抓住轮廓，并承认缺失细节。

intro.en: Approximate is a borrowed Latin participle. English forms approximately, approximation and the technical approximant with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: approximate 是借入的拉丁分词。英语用普通后缀构成 approximately、approximation 和技术词 approximant。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on prope 'near': proximus 'nearest', proximare 'come near', and approximare 'approach'. The same root gives proximity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族建立在 prope“近”上：proximus“最近的”、proximare“靠近”、approximare“接近”。同一词根给出 proximity。

items.meaning: about; roughly
items.example: The trip takes approximately two hours.
items.exampleCN: 这趟行程大约需要两小时。

items.meaning: a result or description that is close but not exact
items.example: The first approximation was too crude.
items.exampleCN: 最初的近似太粗糙了。

items.meaning: more than one approximate result
items.example: Successive approximations improved the model.
items.exampleCN: 逐次近似让模型不断改进。

items.meaning: tending to approximate; not exact
items.meaningCN: 近似的；带有近似性质的
items.example: The approximative method is good enough for planning.
items.exampleCN: 这种近似方法用于规划已经足够。

items.meaning: in phonetics, a speech sound made with little obstruction
items.example: The sound /r/ is often an approximant.
items.exampleCN: /r/ 常常是近音。

items.meaning: estimated or came near in the past
items.meaningCN: 已估算；曾接近（过去式/过去分词）
items.example: The curve was approximated by a straight line.
items.exampleCN: 这条曲线被一条直线近似了。

items.meaning: estimating or coming near
items.example: The software is approximating the missing values.
items.exampleCN: 软件正在估算缺失值。

items.meaning: able to be approximated
items.example: The function is approximable near zero.
items.exampleCN: 这个函数在零附近可以被近似。

definition_en: based on personal choice or whim rather than reason, rules, or evidence
core_image: 法官抛硬币定案，没有可循的规则
scene: The referee was booed for an arbitrary decision: the same move had not been punished in the previous match.
sceneCN: 这里 arbitrary 是「武断的、缺乏依据的」（第 2 个义项：决定没有规则或证据支撑）；句意：裁判因一次武断判罚被观众嘘，同样的动作在上一场却没有被处罚。场景要点：裁判、观众嘘声、相同动作、前后不一的判罚。

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Random, with no pattern
senses.definition: chosen or arranged without a rule or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 没有规则或模式地选择、排列
senses.example: The files were listed in an arbitrary order.
senses.exampleCN: 文件按任意顺序排列。
senses.why: Latin arbitrarius meant 'depending on the judgment of an arbiter'. When no rule guides the judgment, the result looks random.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 arbitrarius 意为“取决于裁断者的判断”。当没有规则引导判断时，结果就显得随机。

senses.title: Unfounded: a decision without reasons
senses.definition: based on personal opinion or whim rather than evidence or reason
senses.definitionCN: 基于个人意见或一时兴起，而非证据或理性
senses.example: The selection seemed arbitrary because no criteria were published.
senses.exampleCN: 因为没公布标准，这次选拔显得很武断。
senses.why: An arbiter may decide without a stated rule. When the decision affects others and gives no reasons, 'judgment' becomes 'arbitrary'.
senses.whyCN: 裁断者可以在没有明示规则的情况下决定。当这个决定影响他人又不给理由时，“判断”就变成了“武断”。

senses.title: Despotic: power without limits
senses.definition: using power in an unrestrained way, without checks or consent
senses.definitionCN: 不受制约、不征得同意地行使权力
senses.example: The citizens protested against arbitrary rule.
senses.exampleCN: 市民抗议专断统治。
senses.why: When the arbiter is also the ruler and no law binds them, personal judgment becomes political tyranny.
senses.whyCN: 当裁断者同时是统治者、又没有法律约束时，个人判断就变成政治上的专断。

senses.title: Decided by will, not by law
senses.definition: determined by a person's will rather than by law, custom, or objective standard
senses.definitionCN: 由个人意志而非法律、习俗或客观标准决定
senses.example: The boundary was arbitrary, drawn without consulting the villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这条边界是任意划的，没有征求村庄意见。
senses.why: The word contrasts with certus, 'fixed'. What is arbitrary is not fixed by anything outside the decider's will.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与 certus“固定的”相对。任意的东西，不是由决定者意志之外的任何东西固定下来的。

senses.title: Mathematics: an arbitrary choice
senses.definition: in mathematics, chosen freely for a proof because the result does not depend on the specific choice
senses.definitionCN: 数学中，因结果不依赖具体选择而可自由选取的
senses.example: Let x be an arbitrary positive number.
senses.exampleCN: 设 x 为任意正数。
senses.why: Mathematics neutralizes the negative sense: if a proof works for any choice, arbitrariness becomes generality.
senses.whyCN: 数学把贬义中性化了：如果证明对任何选择都成立，任意性就变成了普遍性。

senses.title: Legal: left to an arbitrator's discretion
senses.definition: in law or arbitration, left to the judgment of an appointed decision-maker
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或仲裁中，交由被指定的裁断者判断
senses.example: The penalty was arbitrary within the limits set by the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 罚则在合同规定的范围内由仲裁者裁量。
senses.why: Arbitration keeps the old neutral meaning: a decision entrusted to a judge or umpire rather than fixed by a formula.
senses.whyCN: 仲裁保留了古老的中性含义：决定托付给法官或公断人，而不是由公式固定。

senses.title: Linguistics: the arbitrary sign
senses.definition: in linguistics, the principle that the sound of a word is not naturally tied to its meaning
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中，词的语音与意义之间没有自然必然联系
senses.example: Saussure argued that the sign is arbitrary.
senses.exampleCN: 索绪尔主张语言符号具有任意性。
senses.why: Here 'no natural rule' is a technical claim, not a criticism. Different languages can use different sounds for the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“没有自然规则”是技术主张，不是批评。不同语言可以用不同声音指同一事物。

senses.title: Arbitrary arrest or detention
senses.definition: in human rights law, arrest or detention without legal basis or fair procedure
senses.definitionCN: 人权法中，缺乏法律依据或正当程序的逮捕或拘押
senses.example: The report documented arbitrary detention of journalists.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了记者遭到任意拘押的情况。
senses.why: The political sense becomes a legal category: a state act that is not bound by law is 'arbitrary' in international usage.
senses.whyCN: 政治义变成法律类别：不受法律约束的国家行为，在国际用法中就是 arbitrary。

intro.en: Arbitrary came straight from Latin and was originally neutral. Its negative political sense is a later English development.
intro.cn: arbitrary 直接从拉丁语借入，最初是中性的。它贬义的政治含义是英语后来发展出来的。

items.en: First recorded around 1400, borrowed directly from Latin arbitrarius rather than through French.
items.cn: 约 1400 年最早记录，直接从拉丁语 arbitrarius 借入，没有经过法语。

items.en: arbitrarius meant 'depending on the will of an arbiter, discretionary'. It was neutral: a decision made by a judge or umpire.
items.cn: arbitrarius 意为“取决于裁断者意志的、可裁量的”。它当时是中性的：由法官或公断人作出的决定。

items.en: arbiter meant 'judge, umpire, mediator', literally 'one who goes to see or decide'. The word was built with ad- 'to' and a verb baetere 'to go'.
items.cn: arbiter 意为“法官、公断人、调解人”，字面是“前去看或裁断的人”。它由 ad-“向”和动词 baetere“走”构成。

items.en: The verb baetere is of uncertain origin; de Vaan records variants baetō, bētō and -bītō. The internal etymology of arbiter is therefore not fully settled.
items.cn: 动词 baetere 的词源不确定；de Vaan 记录了 baetō、bētō、-bītō 等变体。因此 arbiter 的内部词源尚无定论。

items.en: The neutral sense 'discretionary' survives in legal and mathematical uses. The negative sense 'despotic, capricious' becomes common in the 1640s, especially in phrases such as arbitrary government.
items.cn: 中性的“可裁量”义保留在法律和数学用法中。贬义的“专断、任性”义在 17 世纪 40 年代变得常见，尤见于 arbitrary government 之类短语。

items.en: Modern English usually uses arbitrary as a criticism, except in mathematics and linguistics, where it is a neutral technical term.
items.cn: 现代英语通常把 arbitrary 用作批评，只有数学和语言学中是中性术语。

note.en: The look-alike group is the arbiter/arbitration family; the meaning group separates randomness, whim and tyranny.
note.cn: 形近组是 arbiter/arbitration 词族；近义组区分随机、任性和暴政。

entries.definition: to settle a dispute as an independent judge. It is the neutral action behind arbiter.
entries.definitionCN: 作为独立裁断者解决争端。它是 arbiter 背后的中性动作。

entries.definition: the process of settling a dispute through an appointed arbitrator
entries.definitionCN: 通过指定的仲裁者解决争端的过程

entries.definition: a person appointed to settle a dispute
entries.definitionCN: 仲裁员；被指定解决争端的人

entries.definition: chosen without a plan or pattern. It is neutral about power and usually about selection, not decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 没有计划或模式地选取。它对权力中性，通常讲选择，不讲决定。

entries.definition: changing suddenly according to whim. It stresses unstable mood, while arbitrary stresses lack of rule.
entries.definitionCN: 随一时兴起突然改变。它强调情绪不定，arbitrary 强调缺乏规则。

entries.definition: ruling with absolute, often cruel power. It is stronger politically than arbitrary.
entries.definitionCN: 以绝对、常带残酷的权力统治。它在政治上比 arbitrary 更强。

entries.definition: not based on facts or evidence. It attacks the basis of a claim, not the process of choosing.
entries.definitionCN: 没有事实或证据依据。它攻击主张的依据，而不是选择的过程。

entries.definition: playful or fanciful in an unpredictable way. It is often lighter and less accusatory than arbitrary.
entries.definitionCN: 以不可预测的方式俏皮或异想天开。它常比 arbitrary 更轻松、更少指责。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: arbiter 'judge', the arbitration family, and the neutral mathematical and linguistic uses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分与同族词：arbiter“裁断者”、arbitration 词族，以及数学和语言学中的中性用法。

normal.en: The root arbiter is a judge. An arbitrary decision is one left to the judge's will, with no fixed rule.
normal.cn: 词根 arbiter 是“裁断者”。arbitrary 决定就是交给裁断者意志、没有固定规则的决定。

normal.en: In mathematics, 'arbitrary' is neutral: let x be an arbitrary number means any number will do.
normal.cn: 在数学中，arbitrary 是中性的：设 x 为任意数，意思是什么数都行。

normal.en: In politics, the same idea turns negative: arbitrary power is power without law.
normal.cn: 在政治中，同一个观念转为贬义：专断权力就是没有法律约束的权力。

normal.en: Arbitrate is the neutral verb; arbitrary is the adjective that often carries criticism.
normal.cn: arbitrate 是中性的动词；arbitrary 是常带批评的形容词。

normal.en: In linguistics, the arbitrary sign means sound and meaning are not naturally linked.
normal.cn: 在语言学中，符号的任意性指语音与意义没有自然联系。

abstract.en: Picture a judge with no law book, only a coin. The decision is still a decision, but nothing outside the judge's hand determines it.
abstract.cn: 想象一位没有法典、只有一枚硬币的法官。决定仍然是决定，但决定者手之外的任何东西都不能决定它。

abstract.en: The word names a gap between a decision and its justification. Fill the gap with law or evidence, and the decision stops being arbitrary.
abstract.cn: 这个词命名的是决定与理由之间的缝隙。用法律或证据填上缝隙，决定就不再是任意的。

abstract.en: Mathematics and linguistics show the neutral face of the same idea: freedom from a rule can be a method, not a failure.
abstract.cn: 数学和语言学展示了同一观念的中性面孔：不受规则约束，可以是一种方法，而不是失败。

examples.en: The teacher's grading seemed arbitrary to the students.
examples.cn: 在学生看来，老师的评分显得很武断。

examples.en: The law protects citizens from arbitrary arrest.
examples.cn: 法律保护公民免受任意逮捕。

examples.en: In the proof, choose an arbitrary point on the line.
examples.cn: 在证明中，任取直线上的一点。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿比吹里”——阿比在里屋吹口哨定规矩，想怎么定就怎么定 → arbitrary 任意的、武断的

root: 源自拉丁语 arbitrarius“取决于裁断者意志的”，词根 arbiter 为“法官、公断人”，核心是“没有外在规则，只凭裁断者意志”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of arbitrary: one idea of decision without an external rule becomes randomness, whim, tyranny, will, mathematical generality, legal discretion, linguistic convention and unlawful detention.
sensesIntro.cn: arbitrary 的八个义项：同一个“决定不受外在规则约束”的观念，变成随机、任性、专断、意志、数学普遍性、法律裁量、语言约定和非法拘押。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a decision is made by will alone, with no rule or evidence outside the decider.
core.cn: 核心意象：决定只由意志作出，决定者之外没有规则或证据。

branches.en: CHOICE: no pattern, and no law or custom fixing the result.
branches.cn: 选择：没有模式，也没有法律或习俗固定结果。

branches.en: JUSTIFICATION: a decision that affects others but offers no reasons.
branches.cn: 理由：影响他人却不给理由的决定。

branches.en: POWER: personal will becomes tyranny, and unlawful state action becomes arbitrary detention.
branches.cn: 权力：个人意志变成暴政，非法国家行为变成任意拘押。

branches.en: NEUTRAL TECHNICAL USES: mathematical generality and linguistic convention.
branches.cn: 中性技术用法：数学的普遍性与语言的约定性。

branches.en: LEGAL DISCRETION: a decision entrusted to an arbitrator rather than a formula.
branches.cn: 法律裁量：决定托付给仲裁者，而不是公式。

intro.en: Arbitrary is a borrowed adjective. English builds the arbitration family and the negative nonarbitrary from it.
intro.cn: arbitrary 是借入的形容词。英语由它构成 arbitration 词族和否定形式 nonarbitrary。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is arbiter 'judge', arbitrarius 'discretionary', arbitrari 'to judge', and arbitrium 'judgment, will'. The internal origin of arbiter is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 arbiter“法官”、arbitrarius“可裁量的”、arbitrari“裁断”、arbitrium“判断、意志”。arbiter 的内部来源不确定。

items.meaning: by will or chance, without a rule
items.example: The names were arbitrarily assigned.
items.exampleCN: 名字是随意分配的。

items.meaning: the quality of being based on will rather than rule
items.example: The arbitrariness of the rules made them hard to follow.
items.exampleCN: 规则太任意，让人难以遵守。

items.meaning: to act as an independent judge in a dispute
items.example: A neutral expert will arbitrate the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 一位中立专家将仲裁这场争端。

items.meaning: the process of settling a dispute through an arbitrator
items.example: The case went to arbitration instead of court.
items.exampleCN: 案件进入仲裁而不是法庭。

items.meaning: a person appointed to settle a dispute
items.example: Each side chose one arbitrator.
items.exampleCN: 双方各选了一名仲裁员。

items.meaning: relating to arbitration
items.example: The arbitral tribunal met in private.
items.exampleCN: 仲裁庭私下开庭。

items.meaning: the decision of an arbitrator; arbitration
items.example: The arbitrament settled the border dispute.
items.exampleCN: 这项裁断解决了边界争端。

items.meaning: able to be settled by arbitration
items.example: Not every dispute is arbitrable.
items.exampleCN: 并非所有争端都可以仲裁。

items.meaning: based on rules or evidence rather than will
items.meaningCN: 非任意的；有规则依据的
items.example: The allocation was nonarbitrary and published in advance.
items.exampleCN: 分配不是任意的，且提前公布。

items.meaning: relating to arbitration
items.example: The arbitrational procedure took six months.
items.exampleCN: 仲裁程序花了六个月。

latinEntries.meaning: depending on an arbiter's will; discretionary
latinEntries.meaningCN: 取决于裁断者意志的；可裁量的

definition_zh: 建筑学；建筑风格；结构；架构
definition_en: the art or practice of designing buildings, or the structure of a complex system
core_image: 先画骨架、再填墙面的蓝图
scene: From the far bank, she studied the building's architecture: its glass walls reflected the whole sky.
sceneCN: 这里 architecture 是「建筑风格、建筑外观」（第 2 个义项：建筑所呈现的风格与形式）；句意：她从对岸打量这座建筑的风格：玻璃幕墙把整片天空都映了进去。场景要点：对岸、玻璃幕墙、映出的天空、建筑整体形式。

forms.label: 复数（多于一个，多用于技术语境）

senses.title: The art and practice of building
senses.definition: the art and science of designing buildings and other structures
senses.definitionCN: 设计建筑及其他结构的艺术与科学
senses.example: She studied architecture in Paris for five years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在巴黎学了五年建筑。
senses.why: Greek arkhitekton meant 'master builder'. Architecture names the whole discipline of the master builder, not a single act of building.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arkhitekton 意为“总建造师”。architecture 命名的是总建造师的整个学科，而不是一次建造动作。

senses.title: The style or character of a building
senses.definition: the style, form, and character of a building or group of buildings
senses.definitionCN: 一座或一组建筑所呈现的风格、形式与特征
senses.example: The city is famous for its Gothic architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市以哥特式建筑闻名。
senses.why: When a discipline produces a building, the building carries the discipline's style. 'Architecture' can therefore name the visible character of a structure.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科造出建筑，建筑就带着这门学科的样式。于是 architecture 也可以命名结构所呈现的特征。

senses.title: The internal structure of a building
senses.definition: the structure and organization of a building's parts
senses.definitionCN: 建筑各部分的构造与组织方式
senses.example: The timber architecture of the roof has survived for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶的木结构已经保存了几个世纪。
senses.why: Behind the surface is a frame. Architecture includes the load-bearing organization that makes a building stand.
senses.whyCN: 表面背后是骨架。architecture 包括让建筑立得住的承重组织。

senses.title: Computer architecture
senses.definition: the design and organization of a computer system's hardware and instruction set
senses.definitionCN: 计算机系统硬件与指令集的设计和组织方式
senses.example: The new chip uses a simpler architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 新芯片采用了更简单的体系结构。
senses.why: A computer is built like a building: a plan, levels, connections, and a load to carry. The metaphor transfers the structural sense.
senses.whyCN: 计算机造得像建筑：有平面、层次、连接和负载。隐喻把“结构”义搬了过去。

senses.title: The architecture of an organization
senses.definition: the structure of roles, rules, and relationships in an organization or system
senses.definitionCN: 组织或系统中角色、规则与关系的结构
senses.example: The reform changed the architecture of the health service.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革改变了医疗服务体系的架构。
senses.why: Institutions have frameworks too. The 'master builder' sense becomes a metaphor for how parts of a system are arranged.
senses.whyCN: 机构也有框架。总建造师的观念变成隐喻，用来指系统各部分如何安排。

senses.title: The overall design or conception
senses.definition: the overall design or plan behind a complex work or system
senses.definitionCN: 复杂作品或系统背后的整体设计与计划
senses.example: The novel's architecture is clear from its chapter titles.
senses.exampleCN: 从章节标题就能看出这部小说的整体构思。
senses.why: Architecture is design before it is material. A poem, a film or a software system can have an architecture: a plan that holds the parts together.
senses.whyCN: architecture 先是设计，然后才是材料。一首诗、一部电影或一套软件都可以有架构：把各部分维系起来的计划。

senses.title: The profession and industry
senses.definition: the profession of architects or the building industry as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 建筑师这一职业或整个建筑行业
senses.example: He works in architecture, not in construction.
senses.exampleCN: 他在建筑设计行业工作，不是施工行业。
senses.why: A discipline becomes a workplace. 'Architecture' can name the people and firms who practice it, distinct from the builders who carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 学科变成职场。architecture 可以命名实践它的群体和公司，与施工者相区别。

senses.title: The built character of a place
senses.titleCN: 城市或景观的建筑面貌
senses.definition: the collective built character of a city, landscape, or neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 城市、景观或街区共同呈现的建筑面貌
senses.example: The architecture of the old quarter is low and dense.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区的建筑面貌低矮而密集。
senses.why: Many buildings together form a larger composition. The word can describe the character of a whole place, not only one structure.
senses.whyCN: 许多建筑共同构成更大的构图。这个词可以描述整个地方的面貌，而不只是一座建筑。

intro.en: Architecture and architect are siblings from Greek, borrowed through French and Latin in the 16th century. Architecture is not English architect plus -ure.
intro.cn: architecture 与 architect 是来自希腊语的兄弟词，16 世纪经法语和拉丁语借入。architecture 不是英语 architect 加 -ure 构成的。

items.en: Architecture is first recorded in the 1560s, borrowed from French architecture, which came from Latin architectura.
items.cn: architecture 最早记录于 1560 年代，借自法语 architecture，后者来自拉丁语 architectura。

items.en: Latin architectura meant 'the art of building', a noun of the art from architectus 'master builder'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 architectura 意为“建造的艺术”，是 architectus“总建造师”的技艺名词。

items.en: Greek arkhitekton 'master builder' = arkhi- 'chief' + tekton 'builder, carpenter'. The arkhi- element is the same one in archon 'ruler'.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhitekton“总建造师”= arkhi-“首席”+ tekton“建造者、木匠”。arkhi- 与 archon“统治者”中的成分相同。

items.en: tekton 'builder, carpenter' goes back to PIE *teks- 'to weave, fabricate'. Building is pictured as joining materials, like weaving.
items.cn: tekton“建造者、木匠”可追溯到原始印欧语 *teks-“编织、制作”。建造被想象成把材料接合起来，像编织一样。

items.en: English architect is also recorded from the 1560s, separately from architecture. Both come from the same Greek root through French and Latin, but neither is derived from the other in English.
items.cn: 英语 architect 同样在 1560 年代有记录，与 architecture 分开借入。两者都经法语和拉丁语来自同一个希腊词根，但在英语中并不是一个由另一个派生。

items.en: Modern English extends architecture from buildings to computers, organizations and works of art. The -ure ending is the Latin -tura, not a productive English suffix.
items.cn: 现代英语把 architecture 从建筑扩展到计算机、组织和艺术作品。-ure 结尾是拉丁语 -tura，不是能产的英语后缀。

note.en: The look-alike group separates architecture from architect and its adjectives; the meaning group separates the art from the thing built.
note.cn: 形近组把 architecture 与 architect 及其形容词分开；近义组区分“设计艺术”与“被建造的东西”。

entries.definition: a person who designs buildings. It is a sibling borrowing, not a shortened form of architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 设计建筑的人。它是平行借入的兄弟词，不是 architecture 的缩写。

entries.definition: relating to architecture or architects
entries.definitionCN: 建筑的；建筑学的（形容词）

entries.definition: in architectural terms; from an architectural point of view
entries.definitionCN: 在建筑上；从建筑角度

entries.definition: a structure with walls and a roof. It is the thing made, not the art of making it.
entries.definitionCN: 有墙和屋顶的结构。它是被造出的物，不是建造的艺术。

entries.definition: the arrangement or organization of parts. It overlaps with architecture's structural sense but lacks the aesthetic discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分的排列或组织。它与 architecture 的结构义重叠，但缺少审美学科含义。

entries.definition: the plan or arrangement of a thing before it is made. It is broader than architecture and applies to any made object.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被造出前的计划或安排。它比 architecture 宽泛，适用于任何人造物。

entries.definition: the act or process of building. It is the making, while architecture is the designing.
entries.definitionCN: 建造的行为或过程。它是“造”，而 architecture 是“设计”。

entries.definition: a supporting structure or set of rules. It matches the organizational sense of architecture.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑性结构或规则体系。它对应 architecture 的组织架构义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek arkhi- 'chief' + tekton 'builder', plus architect, architectural and architectonics.
normalIntro.cn: 真实成分与同族词：希腊语 arkhi-“首席”+ tekton“建造者”，以及 architect、architectural、architectonics。

normal.en: arkhi- is 'chief', tekton is 'builder'. Architecture began as the work of the master builder.
normal.cn: arkhi- 是“首席”，tekton 是“建造者”。architecture 最初是总建造师的工作。

normal.en: An architect designs; architecture is the discipline and the result.
normal.cn: architect 设计；architecture 是学科，也是结果。

normal.en: Architectural is the adjective: architectural drawings, architectural history.
normal.cn: architectural 是形容词：建筑图纸、建筑史。

normal.en: Computer architecture borrows the building metaphor: levels, connections, and a structure that carries load.
normal.cn: 计算机体系结构借用了建筑隐喻：层次、连接，以及承重的结构。

normal.en: Architecture is not 'architect + ure' in English; both words came separately from Greek.
normal.cn: 在英语中 architecture 不是“architect + ure”；两个词是分别从希腊语来的。

abstract.en: Picture a blueprint drawn before any wall exists: lines for the frame, the rooms, the loads. Architecture is the plan that makes the building possible.
abstract.cn: 想象一张在任何墙存在之前画好的蓝图：骨架、房间、承重的线条。architecture 是让建筑成为可能的计划。

abstract.en: The same plan can be made of stone, code, roles or chapters. The material changes; the architecture is the arrangement.
abstract.cn: 同一个计划可以用石头、代码、角色或章节来实现。材料在变，architecture 是那个安排。

abstract.en: A building can be seen; an architecture can be understood. The word moves between the visible style and the invisible order that holds it up.
abstract.cn: 一座建筑可以被看见；一套 architecture 可以被理解。这个词在可见的风格与支撑它的不可见秩序之间移动。

examples.en: The museum is a fine example of modern architecture.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆是现代建筑的佳作。

examples.en: The software's architecture makes it easy to add new features.
examples.cn: 这套软件的架构让它容易增加新功能。

examples.en: She teaches architecture at the university.
examples.cn: 她在大学教建筑学。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿基泰克车”——阿基在泰克车上先画骨架再砌墙，造出一座楼 → architecture 建筑学

root: 源自希腊语 arkhitekton“总建造师”（arkhi-“首席”+ tekton“建造者”），经拉丁语 architectura 与法语进入英语，核心是“先有整体骨架，再有建筑”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of architecture: one idea of a master plan holding parts together applies to buildings, styles, frames, computers, organizations, artworks, professions and whole places.
sensesIntro.cn: architecture 的八个义项：同一个“总体计划维系各部分”的观念，用于建筑、风格、骨架、计算机、组织、作品、行业和整个地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a master plan is drawn first, and parts are arranged to carry the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：先画出总体计划，再安排各部分来承载整体。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND PROFESSION: the art of building, and the industry that practices it.
branches.cn: 学科与行业：建造的艺术，以及实践它的行业。

branches.en: VISIBLE CHARACTER: the style of one building, or the collective look of a place.
branches.cn: 可见特征：一座建筑的风格，或一个地方的整体面貌。

branches.en: PHYSICAL FRAME: the load-bearing structure behind the surface.
branches.cn: 物理骨架：表面背后的承重结构。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: computers and organizations are arranged like buildings, with levels and connections.
branches.cn: 系统：计算机与组织像建筑一样被安排，有层次和连接。

branches.en: OVERALL DESIGN: any complex work can have an architecture of parts.
branches.cn: 整体设计：任何复杂作品都可以有由部分构成的架构。

intro.en: Architecture is a Greek-derived noun. English adds -al and -ally to architect, and uses architecture in compounds such as landscape architecture.
intro.cn: architecture 是希腊来源的名词。英语给 architect 加 -al、-ally，并用 architecture 构成 landscape architecture 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is architectura 'the art of building' and architectus 'master builder', both from Greek arkhitekton. The Greek elements are arkhi- 'chief' and tekton 'builder'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 architectura“建造艺术”和 architectus“总建造师”，两者都来自希腊语 arkhitekton。希腊成分是 arkhi-“首席”和 tekton“建造者”。

items.meaning: a person who designs buildings
items.example: The architect presented three possible designs.
items.exampleCN: 建筑师提出了三种可能的设计。

items.meaning: more than one architect
items.example: The two architects disagreed about the roof.
items.exampleCN: 两位建筑师对屋顶意见不一。

items.meaning: relating to architecture
items.example: The plan has great architectural value.
items.exampleCN: 这份方案具有很高的建筑价值。

items.meaning: from an architectural point of view
items.meaningCN: 从建筑角度看；在建筑上
items.example: The two buildings are architecturally different.
items.exampleCN: 这两座建筑在建筑风格上不同。

items.meaning: relating to architecture or to the systematic arrangement of knowledge
items.meaningCN: 建筑学的；体系构造的（较学术）
items.example: The book has an architectonic structure.
items.exampleCN: 这本书有严整的体系结构。

items.meaning: the science of architecture or of systematic structure
items.meaningCN: 建筑学；结构学；体系构造学
items.example: Kant wrote about the architectonics of reason.
items.exampleCN: 康德论述了理性的体系构造。

items.meaning: more than one architectural system, especially in computing
items.meaningCN: 多种架构（复数，多用于计算机语境）
items.example: The software supports several hardware architectures.
items.exampleCN: 这套软件支持多种硬件架构。

items.meaning: the design of outdoor spaces and gardens
items.example: Landscape architecture shaped the park's paths.
items.exampleCN: 景观设计塑造了公园的步道。

items.meaning: the design and organization of a computer system
items.example: The course covers computer architecture and memory.
items.exampleCN: 这门课讲授计算机体系结构与存储。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 统治者；首席长官（与 arkhi- 同源）
